tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

content.content:
1	# Feature Specification: P-RF01 — Multimodal capture
2	
3	**Feature Branch**: `003-multimodal-capture` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)
4	
5	**Created**: 2026-10-12
6	
7	**Status**: Draft
8	
9	**Input**: User description: "P-RF01 — Multimodal capture: Let the user create a journal entry by text, audio recording or photo, from the Insertion Modal, per docs/input/requirements.md section 1 (RF01) and its acceptance criteria. Prototype states: Insertion modal — 'Texto', 'Áudio — Gravando', 'Foto — Captura' (prototype extract, section 2.3), opened by the '+' button of Home/Chat. Backend: POST /entries with source manual/audio/photo. Depends on F000, RF03. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements section 2), or change the backend."
10	
11	## Clarifications
12	
13	### Session 2026-10-12
14	
15	- Q: When a user stops recording audio or captures a photo in this unit, how should Save behave, given RF02 (speech-to-text/OCR) is an explicitly later unit and the prototype states listed for this unit stop at "Gravando" and "Captura"? → A: RF01 performs the minimal on-device transcription (audio) or backend OCR call (photo) needed to produce text content inline, as part of confirming Save, shown with only a plain/generic loading indicator — not RF02's dedicated "Processando / Transcrito / Reconhecido / Erro" screens, their editable-text review step, or their specific retry affordances ("Tentar novamente", "Salvar só a foto"). This is the only reading under which RF01 alone satisfies its own stated acceptance criterion that all three modalities "result in the same persisted-entry format," since entries are immutable (no `PATCH`/`DELETE /entries/:id`) and therefore cannot be corrected after creation — recognition must happen before the entry exists. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I, where the input docs are silent on this exact boundary.)
16	- Q: After a successful Save, the modal closes back to Home/Chat — but Home/Chat never renders journal entries (those appear only in the later "Meus Registros" unit, RF07). What should FR-011's "reflected in the app's state" actually look like on Home/Chat itself? → A: Nothing new is shown on Home/Chat. The prototype documents no confirmation screen, toast, or any other on-screen change for this flow, and inventing one would conflict with Principle IV's visual-fidelity constraint (faithfulness to a frozen prototype that defines no such state) as well as SC-003's "no required intermediate screens." "Reflected in the app's state" means only that the newly created entry is added to the app's local entries store/cache — the same store later units (e.g., RF07) will read from — not that Home/Chat's UI changes in any visible way. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principles I and IV, where the input docs are silent on this exact boundary.)
17	- Q: The backend's `POST /media/ocr` response carries a `confidence: "high"|"low"` field alongside the recognized text — does a `low`-confidence recognition get treated any differently from `high`-confidence before Save completes? → A: No. This unit's scope (FR-007) stops at automatically producing recognized text before Save; any quality gating, warning, or review step keyed to confidence is exactly the kind of recognition-quality handling RF02 owns (its "Transcrito"/"Reconhecido" review states, deliberately deferred here). Confidence is therefore ignored in this unit: any non-empty recognized text, regardless of confidence, proceeds to Save normally; only the already-specified zero-usable-text case (Edge Cases) is treated as a failure. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I, where the input docs are silent on this exact boundary.)
18	
19	## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
20	
21	### User Story 1 - Writing a journal entry as text (Priority: P1)
22	
23	A user wants to quickly note something in words. They tap "+" on Home/Chat, the Insertion Modal opens on its "Texto" tab, they write freely in the text field, and tap "Salvar". The modal closes and the note now exists as one of their journal entries.
24	
25	**Why this priority**: The simplest and fully self-contained of the three capture paths — it has no dependency on recognition of any kind, so it is the first thing that must work end to end.
26	
27	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by tapping "+", typing text into the Texto tab, tapping "Salvar", and confirming a new entry with that exact text and origin "manual" now exists, and the modal has closed back to Home/Chat.
28	
29	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
30	
31	1. **Given** Home/Chat is open, **When** the user taps "+", **Then** the Insertion Modal opens as an overlay on top of Home/Chat (which stays in place underneath), defaulted to the "Texto" tab with an empty field.
32	2. **Given** the Texto tab with text typed into the field, **When** the user taps "Salvar", **Then** a new journal entry is created with that text as its content and origin "manual", and the modal closes, returning to Home/Chat.
33	3. **Given** the Texto tab with an empty field, **When** the user looks at "Salvar", **Then** the action is unavailable (disabled), so an empty entry can never be created.
34	
35	---
36	
37	### User Story 2 - Recording a journal entry as audio (Priority: P1)
38	
39	A user prefers to speak rather than type. They tap "+", switch to the "Áudio" tab, and recording begins with a visible waveform and timer. They tap stop, and after a brief moment the spoken content is saved as a journal entry just like a written one.
40	
41	**Why this priority**: Voice capture is one of the two microphone/camera-dependent paths and, together with Story 1, establishes that every modality converges on the same entry format — the central acceptance criterion of this unit.
42	
43	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by opening the Áudio tab, recording a short spoken note, stopping the recording, confirming Save completes, and confirming a new entry exists with origin "audio" and text content derived from what was spoken.
44	
45	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
46	
47	1. **Given** the Insertion Modal is open, **When** the user switches to the "Áudio" tab, **Then** recording starts immediately, showing a stop control, an animated waveform, and a running mm:ss timer.
48	2. **Given** an active recording, **When** the user taps stop, **Then** the recording ends and the system automatically transcribes it and completes the save as part of confirming the capture, producing one new entry with origin "audio" and the transcribed text as its content.
49	3. **Given** a completed audio capture that is being transcribed and saved, **When** that processing is underway, **Then** the user sees a plain loading indicator (not a detailed multi-state screen) until it finishes.
50	4. **Given** transcription or the save itself fails (e.g., inaudible recording, network timeout), **When** that happens, **Then** no entry is created, a clear failure message is shown, and the user can retry without having to re-record, as long as the captured audio is still held locally.
51	
52	---
53	
54	### User Story 3 - Capturing a journal entry from a photo (Priority: P2)
55	
56	A user has something written down on paper, a receipt, or a whiteboard. They tap "+", switch to the "Foto" tab, choose "Câmera" or "Galeria", and the text in the image becomes a journal entry.
57	
58	**Why this priority**: Mirrors Story 2's recognition pipeline for a second input type; ordered after audio because the text-recognition concern it shares with Story 2 is already established there.
59	
60	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by opening the Foto tab, choosing "Câmera" or "Galeria" to supply an image containing legible text, confirming the save completes, and confirming a new entry exists with origin "photo" and the recognized text as its content.
61	
62	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
63	
64	1. **Given** the Insertion Modal is open, **When** the user switches to the "Foto" tab, **Then** two options are shown — "Câmera" and "Galeria" — with no image selected yet.
65	2. **Given** the user picks "Câmera" or "Galeria" and supplies an image, **When** that image is provided, **Then** the system automatically extracts its text and completes the save as part of confirming the capture, producing one new entry with origin "photo" and the recognized text as its content.
66	3. **Given** a completed photo capture that is being recognized and saved, **When** that processing is underway, **Then** the user sees a plain loading indicator (not a detailed multi-state screen) until it finishes.
67	4. **Given** text recognition or the save itself fails, **When** that happens, **Then** no entry is created, a clear failure message is shown, and the user can retry without having to recapture the image, as long as it is still held locally.
68	
69	---
70	
71	### User Story 4 - Abandoning a capture leaves nothing behind (Priority: P3)
72	
73	A user starts writing, recording, or photographing, changes their mind, and backs out. Nothing about that attempt is saved anywhere.
74	
75	**Why this priority**: A safety property that applies across all three modalities rather than a feature of its own; depends on Stories 1–3 already existing to have something to abandon.
76	
77	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by starting each modality (typing a partial note, starting a recording, opening the camera/gallery picker) and closing the modal or navigating away before tapping Salvar, then confirming no new entry was created in any case.
78	
79	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
80	
81	1. **Given** partially typed text in the Texto tab, **When** the user closes the modal without tapping "Salvar", **Then** no entry is created and the draft text is discarded.
82	2. **Given** an in-progress audio recording, **When** the user closes the modal or stops without confirming save, **Then** no entry is created and no partially-recorded audio is persisted as an entry.
83	3. **Given** the Foto tab's camera/gallery picker is open, **When** the user cancels it without completing a capture, **Then** no entry is created.
84	
85	---
86	
87	### Edge Cases
88	
89	- Microphone or camera permission is denied at the OS level: the respective tab shows an explanatory message in place of the recording/capture controls, instead of silently failing or crashing.
90	- The user switches tabs while a recording is in progress: the in-progress recording is discarded (same outcome as closing the modal), since no partial entry may survive regardless of which tab is active afterward.
91	- The app is backgrounded or killed while a capture is in progress and unsaved: nothing is lost that mattered, because nothing was persisted yet — on return, the modal reopens to its default empty state.
92	- Transcription or OCR succeeds technically but returns no usable text (e.g., silence, a blank or illegible image): Save fails with a clear message rather than creating an empty or near-empty entry. A `low`-confidence OCR result that still contains text is not treated as a failure — confidence-based quality gating is out of scope for this unit (reserved for RF02) — so Save proceeds normally with whatever text was recognized.
93	- The device is offline when the user taps "Salvar": the save is blocked immediately with a clear message, without attempting a network call that cannot succeed, consistent with this product's cloud-only architecture (no offline writes).
94	- The user double-taps "Salvar": only one entry is ever created per confirmed capture, never duplicates.
95	
96	## Requirements *(mandatory)*
97	
98	### Functional Requirements
99	
100	- **FR-001**: The system MUST provide an Insertion Modal, opened by the "+" button on Home/Chat, shown as an overlay above Home/Chat (with a darkened scrim) without discarding or navigating away from Home/Chat's state underneath.
101	- **FR-002**: The Insertion Modal MUST present exactly three capture modes as tabs — "Texto", "Áudio", "Foto" — with the active tab visually distinguished, and MUST reset every tab to its initial, empty state each time the modal is freshly opened.
102	- **FR-003**: The "Texto" tab MUST provide a free multiline text field and a "Salvar" action that is unavailable while the field is empty.
103	- **FR-004**: The "Áudio" tab MUST start real-time audio recording as soon as it becomes active, showing a stop control, an animated waveform, and a running timer, matching the "Gravando" state.
104	- **FR-005**: The "Foto" tab MUST offer the user a choice between the device camera and the photo gallery to supply a single image, matching the "Captura" state.
105	- **FR-006**: Confirming Save on any modality MUST result in exactly one persisted journal entry, created through the entry-creation endpoint, carrying the content appropriate to that modality and the correct origin (`manual` for text, `audio` for audio, `photo` for photo) — never a chat message.
106	- **FR-007**: For the audio and photo modalities, confirming Save MUST automatically produce the text content the entry requires — via on-device transcription for audio and backend text recognition for photo — before the entry is created, shown to the user only as a plain, generic loading indicator while it happens; this unit MUST NOT present a dedicated multi-state screen (distinct "processing", "transcribed"/"recognized", or "error" states with their own styling), an editable review step for the recognized text, or modality-specific retry affordances such as "Tentar novamente" or "Salvar só a foto" — those are reserved for a later unit.
107	- **FR-008**: If a capture is abandoned before Save is confirmed — the modal is closed, the user navigates away, a recording is stopped without saving, or an in-progress camera/gallery selection is cancelled — the system MUST NOT create any entry, partial or empty, for that capture.
108	- **FR-009**: If recognizing audio or photo content fails, or the entry-creation call itself fails, when Save is attempted, the system MUST NOT create a partial or placeholder entry; it MUST show a clear failure indication and let the user retry the same captured audio or image without requiring a fresh recording or photo, as long as that captured content is still held locally.
109	- **FR-010**: Creating an entry MUST require network connectivity; when the device is offline, the system MUST block the Save action with a clear message rather than attempting a write that cannot succeed.

112	- **FR-013**: This unit MUST NOT modify the backend, its API contract, or its configuration in any way.

116	- **Journal Entry**: A persisted record with text content, an origin (`manual`, `audio`, or `photo` for this unit), and a creation time; structurally identical regardless of which modality produced it, and immutable once created.
117	- **Capture Session**: Ephemeral, device-only state that exists only while the Insertion Modal is open — which tab is active, any in-progress recording or selected image, and text recognized but not yet saved. It is entirely discarded if the capture is abandoned, and never itself becomes a persisted entry.

122	
123	- **SC-001**: 100% of successfully saved captures, across all three modalities, produce a journal entry that is structurally identical to the others (differing only in its content and origin) — none is treated as a special case downstream.
124	- **SC-002**: 100% of abandoned captures (modal closed, navigation away, in-progress recording stopped without saving, or picker cancelled) leave zero entries behind.
125	- **SC-003**: Users can go from tapping "+" to a newly saved text entry in well under 15 seconds of their own interaction time (typing and one tap), with no required intermediate screens.
126	- **SC-004**: A failure recognizing or saving audio or photo content never forces the user to redo the recording or recapture the photo while that captured content is still available — 0% of such failures result in lost source material.
127	- **SC-005**: 100% of save attempts made while offline are blocked with a clear message before any network call is attempted.
128	
129	## Assumptions
130	
131	- The "Áudio" tab begins recording automatically as soon as it becomes the active tab (matching the prototype, which shows "Gravando" as that tab's default state), requesting microphone permission at that point if not already granted.
132	- Audio transcription runs on-device (per the project's fixed technology stack) and photo text recognition runs via the backend's existing OCR endpoint (which does not persist the image); invoking both is a use of already-established, fixed stack pieces rather than new functionality reserved for RF02 — only RF02's dedicated multi-state UI, editable review, and modality-specific retry/fallback actions are deferred, per the resolved Clarification above.

# Feature Specification: P-RF01 — Multimodal capture

**Feature Branch**: `003-multimodal-capture` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)

**Created**: 2026-10-12

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User description: "P-RF01 — Multimodal capture: Let the user create a journal entry by text, audio recording or photo, from the Insertion Modal, per docs/input/requirements.md section 1 (RF01) and its acceptance criteria. Prototype states: Insertion modal — 'Texto', 'Áudio — Gravando', 'Foto — Captura' (prototype extract, section 2.3), opened by the '+' button of Home/Chat. Backend: POST /entries with source manual/audio/photo. Depends on F000, RF03. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements section 2), or change the backend."

## Clarifications

### Session 2026-10-12

- Q: When a user stops recording audio or captures a photo in this unit, how should Save behave, given RF02 (speech-to-text/OCR) is an explicitly later unit and the prototype states listed for this unit stop at "Gravando" and "Captura"? → A: RF01 performs the minimal on-device transcription (audio) or backend OCR call (photo) needed to produce text content inline, as part of confirming Save, shown with only a plain/generic loading indicator — not RF02's dedicated "Processando / Transcrito / Reconhecido / Erro" screens, their editable-text review step, or their specific retry affordances ("Tentar novamente", "Salvar só a foto"). This is the only reading under which RF01 alone satisfies its own stated acceptance criterion that all three modalities "result in the same persisted-entry format," since entries are immutable (no `PATCH`/`DELETE /entries/:id`) and therefore cannot be corrected after creation — recognition must happen before the entry exists. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I, where the input docs are silent on this exact boundary.)
- Q: After a successful Save, the modal closes back to Home/Chat — but Home/Chat never renders journal entries (those appear only in the later "Meus Registros" unit, RF07). What should FR-011's "reflected in the app's state" actually look like on Home/Chat itself? → A: Nothing new is shown on Home/Chat. The prototype documents no confirmation screen, toast, or any other on-screen change for this flow, and inventing one would conflict with Principle IV's visual-fidelity constraint (faithfulness to a frozen prototype that defines no such state) as well as SC-003's "no required intermediate screens." "Reflected in the app's state" means only that the newly created entry is added to the app's local entries store/cache — the same store later units (e.g., RF07) will read from — not that Home/Chat's UI changes in any visible way. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principles I and IV, where the input docs are silent on this exact boundary.)
- Q: The backend's `POST /media/ocr` response carries a `confidence: "high"|"low"` field alongside the recognized text — does a `low`-confidence recognition get treated any differently from `high`-confidence before Save completes? → A: No. This unit's scope (FR-007) stops at automatically producing recognized text before Save; any quality gating, warning, or review step keyed to confidence is exactly the kind of recognition-quality handling RF02 owns (its "Transcrito"/"Reconhecido" review states, deliberately deferred here). Confidence is therefore ignored in this unit: any non-empty recognized text, regardless of confidence, proceeds to Save normally; only the already-specified zero-usable-text case (Edge Cases) is treated as a failure. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I, where the input docs are silent on this exact boundary.)

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Writing a journal entry as text (Priority: P1)

A user wants to quickly note something in words. They tap "+" on Home/Chat, the Insertion Modal opens on its "Texto" tab, they write freely in the text field, and tap "Salvar". The modal closes and the note now exists as one of their journal entries.

**Why this priority**: The simplest and fully self-contained of the three capture paths — it has no dependency on recognition of any kind, so it is the first thing that must work end to end.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by tapping "+", typing text into the Texto tab, tapping "Salvar", and confirming a new entry with that exact text and origin "manual" now exists, and the modal has closed back to Home/Chat.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** Home/Chat is open, **When** the user taps "+", **Then** the Insertion Modal opens as an overlay on top of Home/Chat (which stays in place underneath), defaulted to the "Texto" tab with an empty field.
2. **Given** the Texto tab with text typed into the field, **When** the user taps "Salvar", **Then** a new journal entry is created with that text as its content and origin "manual", and the modal closes, returning to Home/Chat.
3. **Given** the Texto tab with an empty field, **When** the user looks at "Salvar", **Then** the action is unavailable (disabled), so an empty entry can never be created.

---

### User Story 2 - Recording a journal entry as audio (Priority: P1)

A user prefers to speak rather than type. They tap "+", switch to the "Áudio" tab, and recording begins with a visible waveform and timer. They tap stop, and after a brief moment the spoken content is saved as a journal entry just like a written one.

**Why this priority**: Voice capture is one of the two microphone/camera-dependent paths and, together with Story 1, establishes that every modality converges on the same entry format — the central acceptance criterion of this unit.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by opening the Áudio tab, recording a short spoken note, stopping the recording, confirming Save completes, and confirming a new entry exists with origin "audio" and text content derived from what was spoken.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the Insertion Modal is open, **When** the user switches to the "Áudio" tab, **Then** recording starts immediately, showing a stop control, an animated waveform, and a running mm:ss timer.
2. **Given** an active recording, **When** the user taps stop, **Then** the recording ends and the system automatically transcribes it and completes the save as part of confirming the capture, producing one new entry with origin "audio" and the transcribed text as its content.
3. **Given** a completed audio capture that is being transcribed and saved, **When** that processing is underway, **Then** the user sees a plain loading indicator (not a detailed multi-state screen) until it finishes.
4. **Given** transcription or the save itself fails (e.g., inaudible recording, network timeout), **When** that happens, **Then** no entry is created, a clear failure message is shown, and the user can retry without having to re-record, as long as the captured audio is still held locally.

---

### User Story 3 - Capturing a journal entry from a photo (Priority: P2)

A user has something written down on paper, a receipt, or a whiteboard. They tap "+", switch to the "Foto" tab, choose "Câmera" or "Galeria", and the text in the image becomes a journal entry.

**Why this priority**: Mirrors Story 2's recognition pipeline for a second input type; ordered after audio because the text-recognition concern it shares with Story 2 is already established there.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by opening the Foto tab, choosing "Câmera" or "Galeria" to supply an image containing legible text, confirming the save completes, and confirming a new entry exists with origin "photo" and the recognized text as its content.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the Insertion Modal is open, **When** the user switches to the "Foto" tab, **Then** two options are shown — "Câmera" and "Galeria" — with no image selected yet.
2. **Given** the user picks "Câmera" or "Galeria" and supplies an image, **When** that image is provided, **Then** the system automatically extracts its text and completes the save as part of confirming the capture, producing one new entry with origin "photo" and the recognized text as its content.
3. **Given** a completed photo capture that is being recognized and saved, **When** that processing is underway, **Then** the user sees a plain loading indicator (not a detailed multi-state screen) until it finishes.
4. **Given** text recognition or the save itself fails, **When** that happens, **Then** no entry is created, a clear failure message is shown, and the user can retry without having to recapture the image, as long as it is still held locally.

---

### User Story 4 - Abandoning a capture leaves nothing behind (Priority: P3)

A user starts writing, recording, or photographing, changes their mind, and backs out. Nothing about that attempt is saved anywhere.

**Why this priority**: A safety property that applies across all three modalities rather than a feature of its own; depends on Stories 1–3 already existing to have something to abandon.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by starting each modality (typing a partial note, starting a recording, opening the camera/gallery picker) and closing the modal or navigating away before tapping Salvar, then confirming no new entry was created in any case.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** partially typed text in the Texto tab, **When** the user closes the modal without tapping "Salvar", **Then** no entry is created and the draft text is discarded.
2. **Given** an in-progress audio recording, **When** the user closes the modal or stops without confirming save, **Then** no entry is created and no partially-recorded audio is persisted as an entry.
3. **Given** the Foto tab's camera/gallery picker is open, **When** the user cancels it without completing a capture, **Then** no entry is created.

---

### Edge Cases

- Microphone or camera permission is denied at the OS level: the respective tab shows an explanatory message in place of the recording/capture controls, instead of silently failing or crashing.
- The user switches tabs while a recording is in progress: the in-progress recording is discarded (same outcome as closing the modal), since no partial entry may survive regardless of which tab is active afterward.
- The app is backgrounded or killed while a capture is in progress and unsaved: nothing is lost that mattered, because nothing was persisted yet — on return, the modal reopens to its default empty state.
- Transcription or OCR succeeds technically but returns no usable text (e.g., silence, a blank or illegible image): Save fails with a clear message rather than creating an empty or near-empty entry. A `low`-confidence OCR result that still contains text is not treated as a failure — confidence-based quality gating is out of scope for this unit (reserved for RF02) — so Save proceeds normally with whatever text was recognized.
- The device is offline when the user taps "Salvar": the save is blocked immediately with a clear message, without attempting a network call that cannot succeed, consistent with this product's cloud-only architecture (no offline writes).
- The user double-taps "Salvar": only one entry is ever created per confirmed capture, never duplicates.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: The system MUST provide an Insertion Modal, opened by the "+" button on Home/Chat, shown as an overlay above Home/Chat (with a darkened scrim) without discarding or navigating away from Home/Chat's state underneath.
- **FR-002**: The Insertion Modal MUST present exactly three capture modes as tabs — "Texto", "Áudio", "Foto" — with the active tab visually distinguished, and MUST reset every tab to its initial, empty state each time the modal is freshly opened.
- **FR-003**: The "Texto" tab MUST provide a free multiline text field and a "Salvar" action that is unavailable while the field is empty.
- **FR-004**: The "Áudio" tab MUST start real-time audio recording as soon as it becomes active, showing a stop control, an animated waveform, and a running timer, matching the "Gravando" state.
- **FR-005**: The "Foto" tab MUST offer the user a choice between the device camera and the photo gallery to supply a single image, matching the "Captura" state.
- **FR-006**: Confirming Save on any modality MUST result in exactly one persisted journal entry, created through the entry-creation endpoint, carrying the content appropriate to that modality and the correct origin (`manual` for text, `audio` for audio, `photo` for photo) — never a chat message.
- **FR-007**: For the audio and photo modalities, confirming Save MUST automatically produce the text content the entry requires — via on-device transcription for audio and backend text recognition for photo — before the entry is created, shown to the user only as a plain, generic loading indicator while it happens; this unit MUST NOT present a dedicated multi-state screen (distinct "processing", "transcribed"/"recognized", or "error" states with their own styling), an editable review step for the recognized text, or modality-specific retry affordances such as "Tentar novamente" or "Salvar só a foto" — those are reserved for a later unit.
- **FR-008**: If a capture is abandoned before Save is confirmed — the modal is closed, the user navigates away, a recording is stopped without saving, or an in-progress camera/gallery selection is cancelled — the system MUST NOT create any entry, partial or empty, for that capture.
- **FR-009**: If recognizing audio or photo content fails, or the entry-creation call itself fails, when Save is attempted, the system MUST NOT create a partial or placeholder entry; it MUST show a clear failure indication and let the user retry the same captured audio or image without requiring a fresh recording or photo, as long as that captured content is still held locally.
- **FR-010**: Creating an entry MUST require network connectivity; when the device is offline, the system MUST block the Save action with a clear message rather than attempting a write that cannot succeed.
- **FR-011**: On a successful Save, the Insertion Modal MUST close and return the user to Home/Chat with no other visible change to that screen (the prototype defines no confirmation screen or toast for this flow); the newly created entry MUST be reflected only in the app's local entries store/cache, available for later units (e.g., Meus Registros, RF07) to read.
- **FR-012**: This unit MUST NOT implement any functional behavior belonging to later-delivered requirements (RF02's dedicated recognition-state screens beyond the minimal loading indicator in FR-007, and the full behavior of RF04, RF05, RF06, RF07, RF08, RF09, RF10), nor any extension feature (manual tags/categories, action plans, persona selection).
- **FR-013**: This unit MUST NOT modify the backend, its API contract, or its configuration in any way.

### Key Entities

- **Journal Entry**: A persisted record with text content, an origin (`manual`, `audio`, or `photo` for this unit), and a creation time; structurally identical regardless of which modality produced it, and immutable once created.
- **Capture Session**: Ephemeral, device-only state that exists only while the Insertion Modal is open — which tab is active, any in-progress recording or selected image, and text recognized but not yet saved. It is entirely discarded if the capture is abandoned, and never itself becomes a persisted entry.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: 100% of successfully saved captures, across all three modalities, produce a journal entry that is structurally identical to the others (differing only in its content and origin) — none is treated as a special case downstream.
- **SC-002**: 100% of abandoned captures (modal closed, navigation away, in-progress recording stopped without saving, or picker cancelled) leave zero entries behind.
- **SC-003**: Users can go from tapping "+" to a newly saved text entry in well under 15 seconds of their own interaction time (typing and one tap), with no required intermediate screens.
- **SC-004**: A failure recognizing or saving audio or photo content never forces the user to redo the recording or recapture the photo while that captured content is still available — 0% of such failures result in lost source material.
- **SC-005**: 100% of save attempts made while offline are blocked with a clear message before any network call is attempted.

## Assumptions

- The "Áudio" tab begins recording automatically as soon as it becomes the active tab (matching the prototype, which shows "Gravando" as that tab's default state), requesting microphone permission at that point if not already granted.
- Audio transcription runs on-device (per the project's fixed technology stack) and photo text recognition runs via the backend's existing OCR endpoint (which does not persist the image); invoking both is a use of already-established, fixed stack pieces rather than new functionality reserved for RF02 — only RF02's dedicated multi-state UI, editable review, and modality-specific retry/fallback actions are deferred, per the resolved Clarification above.
- No maximum audio recording duration is defined by the input documents; this unit imposes none beyond ordinary device/storage limits.
- Because entries cannot be edited or deleted after creation, recognition (transcription or OCR) must complete successfully before an entry is created for audio or photo — there is no later correction step in this unit.
- Saving is blocked while offline following the same cloud-only, no-offline-writes pattern already established elsewhere in the product (chat, search); this unit does not introduce an offline queue.
- "Salvar" is treated as idempotent against accidental double-taps (disabled while a save is already in flight) as a standard safeguard, even though the input documents do not call this out explicitly for this requirement the way they do for RF10.
- Switching tabs mid-recording discards the in-progress recording, since the prototype documentation leaves this behavior undefined and no partial entry may survive regardless.

24	# Cerne Constitution
25	
26	## Core Principles
27	
28	### I. Product Source of Truth
29	`docs/input/` — `requirements.md`, `prototype/`, and `backend/` — is the
30	authoritative source for product behavior. `requirements.md` defines
31	functional and quality requirements, screens, the API surface, delivery
32	order, and technical constraints; `prototype/` is the frozen visual
33	reference and its token/state extract; `backend/` documents the existing
34	API, error taxonomy, screen-state map, sync-badge semantics, and fixtures.
35	Where these documents are silent, implementers MUST make a reasonable
36	technical decision rather than block on clarification. Files under
37	`docs/input/` are frozen inputs and MUST NOT be edited by anyone working in
38	this repository.
39	
40	Rationale: a reflective-journaling app with a frozen, already-documented
41	backend has exactly one place where ambiguity should be resolved — the
42	product input — so decisions stay traceable and the backend contract stays
43	stable.
44	
45	### II. Fixed Technology Stack
46	The app is built with Flutter and Dart at the version pinned via `fvm`,
47	using `flutter_bloc` for state management and Clean Architecture with three
48	layers per feature. Error handling MUST use `fpdart`, with every repository
49	returning `Either<Failure, T>`. Test doubles MUST use `mocktail`. Speech-to-
50	text runs on-device via `whisper_ggml`; audio content MUST NEVER be sent to
51	the backend. The shipping platform is iOS. Choices not fixed here — routing,
52	HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics,
53	and charting — are open implementation decisions.
54	
55	Rationale: a single, non-negotiable stack removes a whole category of
56	architectural debate and keeps the codebase consistent across features
57	built by different contributors or at different times.
58	
59	### III. Backend Boundary — Frozen Backend, No Direct AI Calls
60	The backend is already built and frozen. The app consumes it strictly as
61	documented in `docs/input/backend/`, including its API contract
62	(`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`); the app MUST NOT change the
63	backend, its API contract, or its configuration. All AI features, including
64	semantic search, are provided exclusively by the backend — the app MUST
65	NEVER call an AI provider directly. Configuration and credentials come from
66	a project-root `.env` with exactly two variables: `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL` and
67	`SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`. Every call to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<function>` MUST
68	carry the header `apikey: <SUPABASE_ANON_KEY>`. The `Authorization: Bearer`
69	header carries `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` for operations that need no user session
70	(sign-up, login, refresh) and the user's access token for every operation
71	marked `bearerAuth` in the OpenAPI contract. `.env` and any credential MUST
72	NEVER be committed.
73	
74	Rationale: the backend and its AI integrations are out of this project's
75	scope and already relied upon elsewhere; treating them as an immutable,
76	narrowly-accessed contract prevents scope creep and accidental coupling or
77	credential leakage.
78	
79	### IV. Design Token Discipline & Visual Fidelity
80	`lib/core/design_tokens.dart` is the single source of colors, typography,
81	spacing, and radii. No visual value MAY be hardcoded anywhere else. The UI
82	MUST be faithful to `docs/input/prototype/`. UI text MUST be in Portuguese,
83	exactly as written in the prototype; code identifiers, comments, and project
84	documentation MUST be in English.
85	
86	Rationale: a single token source makes visual fidelity (RNF08) mechanically
87	checkable, and separating UI language (Portuguese, matching the frozen
88	prototype) from code language (English) keeps the codebase reviewable while
89	preserving the product's voice.
90	
91	### V. Clean Architecture Folder Convention
92	Code MUST follow the folder convention:
93	```
94	lib/
95	  core/
96	  features/
97	    <feature>/
98	      data/
99	      domain/
100	      presentation/
101	```
102	The domain layer MUST comply with RNF06: zero layer violations — it MUST
103	NOT import `package:flutter` nor any class from a feature's `data/` layer.
104	
105	Rationale: a fixed, enforced folder shape and a flutter/data-free domain
106	layer make the domain independently testable and keep business rules
107	portable regardless of UI or persistence choices.
108	
109	## Quality Standards (RNF01–RNF09)
110	
111	These targets from `docs/input/requirements.md` are binding quality gates:
112	
113	- **RNF01 — Interaction latency**: a local action MUST be reflected in the
114	  UI in under 100 ms; any network call taking longer than 300 ms MUST show a
115	  loading indicator.
116	- **RNF02 — PII stripping**: performed backend-side via Claude Haiku 4.5
117	  with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model; the app
118	  implements no PII-detection logic of its own.
119	- **RNF03 — Zero data retention**: a backend-side policy; the app MUST NOT
120	  introduce its own retention beyond what the backend requires.
121	- **RNF04 — Row Level Security (RLS)**: enforced backend-side; the app MUST
122	  assume RLS is authoritative and MUST NEVER attempt to bypass it.
123	- **RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD)**: the app MUST expose
124	  the account-deletion flow (`DELETE /account`) from Settings.
125	- **RNF06 — Zero layer violations**: see Principle V; 0 violations is the
126	  target.
127	- **RNF07 — Domain test coverage**: `lib/**/domain/**` MUST reach at least
128	  80% test coverage.
129	- **RNF08 — Visual fidelity**: every screen MUST match the prototype's
130	  color, typography, and spacing, with 0 hardcoded visual values outside
131	  `design_tokens.dart`.
132	- **RNF09 — Consistent network-error handling**: every repository MUST use
133	  the `Either<Failure, T>` pattern via `fpdart`; every write endpoint (5
134	  endpoints) MUST handle timeout, malformed response, and no-connection
135	  failures, each covered by `mocktail` tests (15 of 15 scenarios).
136	
137	## Scope & Delivery Boundaries
138	
139	- Functional requirements MUST be implemented in the delivery order given in
140	  `docs/input/requirements.md`.
141	- Extension features (section 2 of `requirements.md`) are explicitly out of
142	  scope and MUST NOT be implemented beyond an optional placeholder menu
143	  entry.
144	- The following actions are prohibited in this repository:
145	  - Changing the backend, its API contract, or its configuration.
146	  - Calling AI providers directly from the app.
147	  - Writing visual values (colors, font sizes, spacing, radii) outside
148	    `design_tokens.dart`.
149	  - Implementing extension features.
150	  - Committing `.env` or any credential.
151	  - Editing files under `docs/input/`.
152	
153	## Governance
154	
155	This constitution supersedes any conflicting practice, template, or
156	instruction used in this repository. Every plan, spec, task list, and
157	review MUST verify compliance with these principles before work is
158	considered done; any deviation MUST be justified in writing in the relevant
159	artifact (plan or PR description) or the work MUST be rejected.
160	
161	**Amendment procedure**: amendments are proposed by editing this file,
162	describing the change and rationale, and are adopted once the project owner
163	accepts the change (commit to this file constitutes adoption in this
164	single-maintainer project). Each amendment MUST update the Sync Impact
165	Report at the top of this file and the version/date line below.
166	
167	**Versioning policy** (semantic versioning for this document):
168	- **MAJOR** — backward-incompatible governance or principle removal/
169	  redefinition.
170	- **MINOR** — a new principle or section added, or materially expanded
171	  guidance.
172	- **PATCH** — wording clarifications, typo fixes, non-semantic refinements.
173	
174	**Compliance review**: any change to `lib/` MUST be checked against the
175	Core Principles and Quality Standards above before merge; violations of
176	RNF06–RNF09 in particular are release blockers.
177	
178	**Version**: 1.0.0 | **Ratified**: 2026-10-11 | **Last Amended**: 2026-10-11

# Cerne Constitution

## Core Principles

### I. Product Source of Truth
`docs/input/` — `requirements.md`, `prototype/`, and `backend/` — is the
authoritative source for product behavior. `requirements.md` defines
functional and quality requirements, screens, the API surface, delivery
order, and technical constraints; `prototype/` is the frozen visual
reference and its token/state extract; `backend/` documents the existing
API, error taxonomy, screen-state map, sync-badge semantics, and fixtures.
Where these documents are silent, implementers MUST make a reasonable
technical decision rather than block on clarification. Files under
`docs/input/` are frozen inputs and MUST NOT be edited by anyone working in
this repository.

Rationale: a reflective-journaling app with a frozen, already-documented
backend has exactly one place where ambiguity should be resolved — the
product input — so decisions stay traceable and the backend contract stays
stable.

### II. Fixed Technology Stack
The app is built with Flutter and Dart at the version pinned via `fvm`,
using `flutter_bloc` for state management and Clean Architecture with three
layers per feature. Error handling MUST use `fpdart`, with every repository
returning `Either<Failure, T>`. Test doubles MUST use `mocktail`. Speech-to-
text runs on-device via `whisper_ggml`; audio content MUST NEVER be sent to
the backend. The shipping platform is iOS. Choices not fixed here — routing,
HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics,
and charting — are open implementation decisions.

Rationale: a single, non-negotiable stack removes a whole category of
architectural debate and keeps the codebase consistent across features
built by different contributors or at different times.

### III. Backend Boundary — Frozen Backend, No Direct AI Calls
The backend is already built and frozen. The app consumes it strictly as
documented in `docs/input/backend/`, including its API contract
(`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`); the app MUST NOT change the
backend, its API contract, or its configuration. All AI features, including
semantic search, are provided exclusively by the backend — the app MUST
NEVER call an AI provider directly. Configuration and credentials come from
a project-root `.env` with exactly two variables: `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL` and
`SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`. Every call to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<function>` MUST
carry the header `apikey: <SUPABASE_ANON_KEY>`. The `Authorization: Bearer`
header carries `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` for operations that need no user session
(sign-up, login, refresh) and the user's access token for every operation
marked `bearerAuth` in the OpenAPI contract. `.env` and any credential MUST
NEVER be committed.

Rationale: the backend and its AI integrations are out of this project's
scope and already relied upon elsewhere; treating them as an immutable,
narrowly-accessed contract prevents scope creep and accidental coupling or
credential leakage.

### IV. Design Token Discipline & Visual Fidelity
`lib/core/design_tokens.dart` is the single source of colors, typography,
spacing, and radii. No visual value MAY be hardcoded anywhere else. The UI
MUST be faithful to `docs/input/prototype/`. UI text MUST be in Portuguese,
exactly as written in the prototype; code identifiers, comments, and project
documentation MUST be in English.

Rationale: a single token source makes visual fidelity (RNF08) mechanically
checkable, and separating UI language (Portuguese, matching the frozen
prototype) from code language (English) keeps the codebase reviewable while
preserving the product's voice.

### V. Clean Architecture Folder Convention
Code MUST follow the folder convention:
```
lib/
  core/
  features/
    <feature>/
      data/
      domain/
      presentation/
```
The domain layer MUST comply with RNF06: zero layer violations — it MUST
NOT import `package:flutter` nor any class from a feature's `data/` layer.

Rationale: a fixed, enforced folder shape and a flutter/data-free domain
layer make the domain independently testable and keep business rules
portable regardless of UI or persistence choices.

## Quality Standards (RNF01–RNF09)

These targets from `docs/input/requirements.md` are binding quality gates:

- **RNF01 — Interaction latency**: a local action MUST be reflected in the
  UI in under 100 ms; any network call taking longer than 300 ms MUST show a
  loading indicator.
- **RNF02 — PII stripping**: performed backend-side via Claude Haiku 4.5
  with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model; the app
  implements no PII-detection logic of its own.
- **RNF03 — Zero data retention**: a backend-side policy; the app MUST NOT
  introduce its own retention beyond what the backend requires.
- **RNF04 — Row Level Security (RLS)**: enforced backend-side; the app MUST
  assume RLS is authoritative and MUST NEVER attempt to bypass it.
- **RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD)**: the app MUST expose
  the account-deletion flow (`DELETE /account`) from Settings.
- **RNF06 — Zero layer violations**: see Principle V; 0 violations is the
  target.
- **RNF07 — Domain test coverage**: `lib/**/domain/**` MUST reach at least
  80% test coverage.
- **RNF08 — Visual fidelity**: every screen MUST match the prototype's
  color, typography, and spacing, with 0 hardcoded visual values outside
  `design_tokens.dart`.
- **RNF09 — Consistent network-error handling**: every repository MUST use
  the `Either<Failure, T>` pattern via `fpdart`; every write endpoint (5
  endpoints) MUST handle timeout, malformed response, and no-connection
  failures, each covered by `mocktail` tests (15 of 15 scenarios).

## Scope & Delivery Boundaries

- Functional requirements MUST be implemented in the delivery order given in
  `docs/input/requirements.md`.
- Extension features (section 2 of `requirements.md`) are explicitly out of
  scope and MUST NOT be implemented beyond an optional placeholder menu
  entry.
- The following actions are prohibited in this repository:
  - Changing the backend, its API contract, or its configuration.
  - Calling AI providers directly from the app.
  - Writing visual values (colors, font sizes, spacing, radii) outside
    `design_tokens.dart`.
  - Implementing extension features.
  - Committing `.env` or any credential.
  - Editing files under `docs/input/`.

## Governance

This constitution supersedes any conflicting practice, template, or
instruction used in this repository. Every plan, spec, task list, and
review MUST verify compliance with these principles before work is
considered done; any deviation MUST be justified in writing in the relevant
artifact (plan or PR description) or the work MUST be rejected.

**Amendment procedure**: amendments are proposed by editing this file,
describing the change and rationale, and are adopted once the project owner
accepts the change (commit to this file constitutes adoption in this
single-maintainer project). Each amendment MUST update the Sync Impact
Report at the top of this file and the version/date line below.

**Versioning policy** (semantic versioning for this document):
- **MAJOR** — backward-incompatible governance or principle removal/
  redefinition.
- **MINOR** — a new principle or section added, or materially expanded
  guidance.
- **PATCH** — wording clarifications, typo fixes, non-semantic refinements.

**Compliance review**: any change to `lib/` MUST be checked against the
Core Principles and Quality Standards above before merge; violations of
RNF06–RNF09 in particular are release blockers.

**Version**: 1.0.0 | **Ratified**: 2026-10-11 | **Last Amended**: 2026-10-11

1	# Cerne — Requirements and Screen Flow
2	
3	Cerne is a reflective-journaling mobile app with an AI assistant. The user records their day by text, audio or photo; a conversational agent consults those records (semantic search) to answer with context and to offer insights.
4	
5	This document is the product specification. The visual reference is the prototype in `docs/input/prototype/`; the backend API is documented in `docs/input/backend/`.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. Functional requirements
10	
11	### RF01 — Multimodal capture (text / audio / photo)
12	Data entry by text, real-time audio recording and photo upload — always through Screen 2 (Insertion Modal), which has a raw text field in addition to the microphone and the gallery. Every capture becomes a persisted record (`POST /entries`), **distinct from a chat message** (see the separation note in RF04).
13	
14	**Acceptance criteria:**
15	- The three modalities (text, audio, photo) result in the same persisted-entry format — none is treated structurally differently from the others after capture.
16	- Cancelling a capture midway (e.g., interrupting a recording) does not create a partial or empty entry.
17	
18	### RF02 — Speech-to-text / OCR processing
19	Transcription of audio (speech-to-text) and recognition of text in images (OCR) over the content captured in RF01.
20	
21	**Acceptance criteria:** four visible states — recording, processing, transcribed, transcription error.
22	
23	### RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
24	Access barrier via Face ID / Touch ID / PIN before exposing the user's data.
25	
26	**Acceptance criteria:**
27	- A biometric failure (e.g., fingerprint not recognized) offers PIN as an alternative, without locking the user out of the app.
28	- The app, sent to the background and resumed after 5 minutes, requires authentication again — it does not stay unlocked indefinitely (fixed value, not configurable by the user).
29	
30	### RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
31	Continuous conversation with the AI agent, with semantic search over previous entries. **Chat messages are conversational and do not create journal entries automatically** — the only exception is the explicit save action described in RF10. Otherwise, the chat queries existing entries via RAG but does not write to them.
32	
33	**Acceptance criteria:**
34	- Three mandatory UI states: processing/streaming, error, complete response.
35	- If the response stream drops midway, the partial message stays visible with a failure indication (it does not disappear).
36	
37	### RF05 — Personal summary export
38	Generation of a narrative summary by AI (Claude Haiku 4.5) from the user's entries, exportable as PDF, with an additional option to download the raw data without the narrative. No clinical or diagnostic connotation. **Scope: job generation, file download and failure handling — never the quality of the generated narrative text.**
39	
40	**Acceptance criteria:**
41	- An export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state (not an empty PDF, not a crash).
42	- A failure generating the narrative text (model timeout) still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure.
43	
44	### RF06 — Semantic search / filter over journal entries
45	Semantic similarity search (via Voyage AI embeddings, reusing the ones already generated in RF01) combined with metadata filters (date, entry type). There is no filter by tag or category: the backend does not implement it in any endpoint — `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` accept only `source` and `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Tags appear only embedded, read-only, in the `Entry` object (see section 2).
46	
47	**Acceptance criteria:**
48	- Searching for a term finds semantically related entries even without the exact word (e.g., searching "ansiedade" returns an entry that only mentions "nervosismo", without the literal term).
49	- 300 ms search debounce: fast typing triggers a single query, not one per keystroke.
50	- Results from the local read cache stay consistent with the server after reconnection, without duplicating displayed items *(the architecture is cloud-only; offline allows only viewing already-cached data, not writing)*.
51	- Two or more filters applied at the same time (`source` + `dateFrom`/`dateTo`) narrow results with AND logic (not OR).
52	- Clearing the filters returns to the full list without restarting the screen.
53	
54	### RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
55	A screen whose state depends simultaneously on authentication, synchronization status and entry data.
56	
57	**Acceptance criteria:**
58	- Session expiration while viewing triggers a new-login prompt without a crash and without losing the scroll position.
59	- The per-entry synchronization status badge updates independently of the authentication stream.
60	- No BLoC imports another BLoC directly.
61	
62	### RF08 — Proactive insights (mechanism)
63	A suggestion inserted into the chat without the user asking for it. **Scope: only the trigger mechanism, never the quality of the generated text.**
64	
65	**Acceptance criteria:**
66	- Trigger after N = 5 user messages OR T = 2 min of inactivity — fires exactly once per satisfied condition.
67	- If insight generation fails (timeout / network error), the main chat keeps working normally.
68	- Dismissing the insight does not change the scroll position or the state of the main conversation.
69	
70	### RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard
71	An evolution chart with a textual summary, computed on demand when the Settings tab is opened. **Scope: aggregation and rendering, never the quality of the narrative text.**
72	
73	**Acceptance criteria:**
74	- Renders correctly in three scenarios: zero entries, one entry, more than 30 entries.
75	- The aggregation recalculates correctly after an entry is created (cache-invalidation test). Entries are immutable: there is no `PATCH /entries/:id` or `DELETE /entries/:id` in the backend, and no screen describes an edit or delete action on an entry.
76	- The AI narrative text is checked only for not breaking the UI in extreme cases — never for its content.
77	
78	### RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry
79	A button on each user message in the chat that converts it into a persisted entry — for moments when the user states relevant information during the conversation, not only through dedicated capture (RF01). It reuses the same `POST /entries` pipeline (PII check + embedding), with the origin marked as `chat`.
80	
81	**Acceptance criteria:**
82	- The chat feature triggers the creation of the entry through a shared interface / use case, never by directly importing a repository or data source of the entries feature — a violation here also breaks RNF06.
83	- Saving the same message twice does not create duplicate entries (idempotency).
84	- A failure to save (network unavailable) keeps the conversation working normally, and the button returns to a state that allows trying again — the same failure-isolation pattern as RF08.
85	- Only user messages have the button — AI responses cannot become entries.
86	
87	---
88	
89	## 2. Extension features — not implemented
90	
91	They keep the "essence" of the original product flow and exist in the prototype, but **receive no functional implementation**. A menu entry may exist as a placeholder.
92	
93	| Original feature | Treatment in the current version |
94	|---|---|
95	| Dynamic categorization (AI) | Simplified to manual tags created by the user (My Records screen) |
96	| Autonomous goal extraction | Action Plans screen — static, no logic |
97	| Dynamic persona adjustment | Simple cosmetic toggle (Settings), low cost to maintain |
98	
99	---
100	
101	## 3. Quality requirements
102	
103	| ID | Requirement | Target |
104	|---|---|---|
105	| RNF06 | Zero layer violations — the domain layer does not import `package:flutter` nor classes from `data/` | 0 violations |
106	| RNF07 | Minimum test coverage of the domain layer (`lib/**/domain/**`) | ≥ 80% |
107	| RNF08 | Visual fidelity to the prototype — the primary color matches the prototype's hex value, typography matches family and size, spacing matches the prototype; no visual value hardcoded outside the central file `design_tokens.dart` | Every screen faithful in color, typography and spacing; 0 hardcoded values |
108	| RNF09 | Consistent network-error handling — `Either<Failure, T>` pattern via `fpdart` in every repository; every write endpoint (5 endpoints) handles three failure types — timeout, malformed response, no connection — covered by tests with `mocktail` | 0 repository signatures outside the pattern; 15 of 15 scenarios handled |
109	
110	## 4. Other non-functional requirements
111	
112	RNF01 — Interaction latency (a local action is reflected in the UI in < 100 ms; any network call above 300 ms shows a loading indicator) · RNF02 — PII stripping (via Claude Haiku 4.5 with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model) · RNF03 — Zero data retention · RNF04 — RLS (Row Level Security) · RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD).
113	
114	**Known limitation:** the system has no protocol for detecting or responding to risk signals (suicidal ideation, self-harm) in entries or chat messages. Since the product is not framed as a mental-health app, this absence is an explicit scope decision.
115	
116	---
117	
118	## 5. Interface architecture and screen flow
119	
120	### 5.1 Visual foundation (design system)
121	Minimalist identity, a warm and neutral palette, readable sans-serif typography, standardized components (buttons, chat bubbles, cards). This foundation is the direct object of RNF08. Tokens: `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md`.
122	
123	### 5.2 Screens
124	
125	**Screen 0 — Splash:** initial loading; checks the connection and syncs the cache in the background. *Connects to: RF06, RNF01.*
126	
127	**Screen 0.1 — Authentication vault:** biometric/PIN barrier before access. *Connects to: RF03.*
128	
129	**Screen 1 — Home (chat):** main screen, continuous conversation, "+" button for multimodal input, AI status indicator, "save to journal" button on each user message. *Connects to: RF04, RF08, RF10, RNF01, RNF09.*
130	
131	**Screen 2 — Insertion Modal:** overlay with three ways to capture — raw text field, microphone (audio) and gallery/camera (photo) — with a transcription indicator. Every capture here creates a persisted entry, never a chat message. *Connects to: RF01, RF02.*
132	
133	**Screen 3 — Side menu (sidebar):** navigation hub, session history, access to My Records / Action Plans / Settings, and a "Novo Chat" button that opens Screen 1 in its empty state. *Connects to: RF04 (via the "Novo Chat" button); the other items are pure navigation.*
134	
135	**Screen 4 — My Records:** consolidated timeline, filters, manual tags (extension, section 2), export. *Connects to: RF07, RF06, RF05.*
136	
137	**Screen 5 — Action Plans:** simple Kanban board (columns "A Fazer" / "Em Andamento" / "Concluído") with static example cards. *(Extension — section 2.)*
138	
139	**Screen 6 — Settings and profile:** evolution dashboard, persona selector — "Analítico" / "Empático" / "Socrático" (extension, section 2; it would only change the system-prompt string of RF04), delete account. *Connects to: RF09, RNF05.*
140	
141	---
142	
143	## 6. Backend endpoint inventory
144	
145	The backend is already built and frozen. The API contract, `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, is the source of truth; this section is a reading of it oriented by screen and requirement. How to build the real URL of each operation: `docs/input/backend/README.md`.
146	
147	Every endpoint returns errors in the standard contract of RNF09 — `{ code, message, retryable }` — and is protected by RLS in Supabase. AI providers: Claude (chat, vision/OCR, summary, insights, dashboard, PII detection) and Voyage AI (embeddings) — the backend's only two external AI dependencies. Audio transcription (speech-to-text) runs on-device (Whisper) and never reaches the backend as an audio file.
148	
149	### 6.1 Authentication and session
150	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
151	|---|---|---|
152	| `POST /auth/signup` | RF03 | — |
153	| `POST /auth/login` | RF03 | — |
154	| `POST /auth/refresh` | RF03, RF07 | — |

# Cerne — Requirements and Screen Flow

Cerne is a reflective-journaling mobile app with an AI assistant. The user records their day by text, audio or photo; a conversational agent consults those records (semantic search) to answer with context and to offer insights.

This document is the product specification. The visual reference is the prototype in `docs/input/prototype/`; the backend API is documented in `docs/input/backend/`.

---

## 1. Functional requirements

### RF01 — Multimodal capture (text / audio / photo)
Data entry by text, real-time audio recording and photo upload — always through Screen 2 (Insertion Modal), which has a raw text field in addition to the microphone and the gallery. Every capture becomes a persisted record (`POST /entries`), **distinct from a chat message** (see the separation note in RF04).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- The three modalities (text, audio, photo) result in the same persisted-entry format — none is treated structurally differently from the others after capture.
- Cancelling a capture midway (e.g., interrupting a recording) does not create a partial or empty entry.

### RF02 — Speech-to-text / OCR processing
Transcription of audio (speech-to-text) and recognition of text in images (OCR) over the content captured in RF01.

**Acceptance criteria:** four visible states — recording, processing, transcribed, transcription error.

### RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
Access barrier via Face ID / Touch ID / PIN before exposing the user's data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- A biometric failure (e.g., fingerprint not recognized) offers PIN as an alternative, without locking the user out of the app.
- The app, sent to the background and resumed after 5 minutes, requires authentication again — it does not stay unlocked indefinitely (fixed value, not configurable by the user).

### RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
Continuous conversation with the AI agent, with semantic search over previous entries. **Chat messages are conversational and do not create journal entries automatically** — the only exception is the explicit save action described in RF10. Otherwise, the chat queries existing entries via RAG but does not write to them.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Three mandatory UI states: processing/streaming, error, complete response.
- If the response stream drops midway, the partial message stays visible with a failure indication (it does not disappear).

### RF05 — Personal summary export
Generation of a narrative summary by AI (Claude Haiku 4.5) from the user's entries, exportable as PDF, with an additional option to download the raw data without the narrative. No clinical or diagnostic connotation. **Scope: job generation, file download and failure handling — never the quality of the generated narrative text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- An export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state (not an empty PDF, not a crash).
- A failure generating the narrative text (model timeout) still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure.

### RF06 — Semantic search / filter over journal entries
Semantic similarity search (via Voyage AI embeddings, reusing the ones already generated in RF01) combined with metadata filters (date, entry type). There is no filter by tag or category: the backend does not implement it in any endpoint — `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` accept only `source` and `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Tags appear only embedded, read-only, in the `Entry` object (see section 2).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Searching for a term finds semantically related entries even without the exact word (e.g., searching "ansiedade" returns an entry that only mentions "nervosismo", without the literal term).
- 300 ms search debounce: fast typing triggers a single query, not one per keystroke.
- Results from the local read cache stay consistent with the server after reconnection, without duplicating displayed items *(the architecture is cloud-only; offline allows only viewing already-cached data, not writing)*.
- Two or more filters applied at the same time (`source` + `dateFrom`/`dateTo`) narrow results with AND logic (not OR).
- Clearing the filters returns to the full list without restarting the screen.

### RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
A screen whose state depends simultaneously on authentication, synchronization status and entry data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Session expiration while viewing triggers a new-login prompt without a crash and without losing the scroll position.
- The per-entry synchronization status badge updates independently of the authentication stream.
- No BLoC imports another BLoC directly.

### RF08 — Proactive insights (mechanism)
A suggestion inserted into the chat without the user asking for it. **Scope: only the trigger mechanism, never the quality of the generated text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Trigger after N = 5 user messages OR T = 2 min of inactivity — fires exactly once per satisfied condition.
- If insight generation fails (timeout / network error), the main chat keeps working normally.
- Dismissing the insight does not change the scroll position or the state of the main conversation.

### RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard
An evolution chart with a textual summary, computed on demand when the Settings tab is opened. **Scope: aggregation and rendering, never the quality of the narrative text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Renders correctly in three scenarios: zero entries, one entry, more than 30 entries.
- The aggregation recalculates correctly after an entry is created (cache-invalidation test). Entries are immutable: there is no `PATCH /entries/:id` or `DELETE /entries/:id` in the backend, and no screen describes an edit or delete action on an entry.
- The AI narrative text is checked only for not breaking the UI in extreme cases — never for its content.

### RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry
A button on each user message in the chat that converts it into a persisted entry — for moments when the user states relevant information during the conversation, not only through dedicated capture (RF01). It reuses the same `POST /entries` pipeline (PII check + embedding), with the origin marked as `chat`.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- The chat feature triggers the creation of the entry through a shared interface / use case, never by directly importing a repository or data source of the entries feature — a violation here also breaks RNF06.
- Saving the same message twice does not create duplicate entries (idempotency).
- A failure to save (network unavailable) keeps the conversation working normally, and the button returns to a state that allows trying again — the same failure-isolation pattern as RF08.
- Only user messages have the button — AI responses cannot become entries.

---

## 2. Extension features — not implemented

They keep the "essence" of the original product flow and exist in the prototype, but **receive no functional implementation**. A menu entry may exist as a placeholder.

| Original feature | Treatment in the current version |
|---|---|
| Dynamic categorization (AI) | Simplified to manual tags created by the user (My Records screen) |
| Autonomous goal extraction | Action Plans screen — static, no logic |
| Dynamic persona adjustment | Simple cosmetic toggle (Settings), low cost to maintain |

---

## 3. Quality requirements

| ID | Requirement | Target |
|---|---|---|
| RNF06 | Zero layer violations — the domain layer does not import `package:flutter` nor classes from `data/` | 0 violations |
| RNF07 | Minimum test coverage of the domain layer (`lib/**/domain/**`) | ≥ 80% |
| RNF08 | Visual fidelity to the prototype — the primary color matches the prototype's hex value, typography matches family and size, spacing matches the prototype; no visual value hardcoded outside the central file `design_tokens.dart` | Every screen faithful in color, typography and spacing; 0 hardcoded values |
| RNF09 | Consistent network-error handling — `Either<Failure, T>` pattern via `fpdart` in every repository; every write endpoint (5 endpoints) handles three failure types — timeout, malformed response, no connection — covered by tests with `mocktail` | 0 repository signatures outside the pattern; 15 of 15 scenarios handled |

## 4. Other non-functional requirements

RNF01 — Interaction latency (a local action is reflected in the UI in < 100 ms; any network call above 300 ms shows a loading indicator) · RNF02 — PII stripping (via Claude Haiku 4.5 with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model) · RNF03 — Zero data retention · RNF04 — RLS (Row Level Security) · RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD).

**Known limitation:** the system has no protocol for detecting or responding to risk signals (suicidal ideation, self-harm) in entries or chat messages. Since the product is not framed as a mental-health app, this absence is an explicit scope decision.

---

## 5. Interface architecture and screen flow

### 5.1 Visual foundation (design system)
Minimalist identity, a warm and neutral palette, readable sans-serif typography, standardized components (buttons, chat bubbles, cards). This foundation is the direct object of RNF08. Tokens: `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md`.

### 5.2 Screens

**Screen 0 — Splash:** initial loading; checks the connection and syncs the cache in the background. *Connects to: RF06, RNF01.*

**Screen 0.1 — Authentication vault:** biometric/PIN barrier before access. *Connects to: RF03.*

**Screen 1 — Home (chat):** main screen, continuous conversation, "+" button for multimodal input, AI status indicator, "save to journal" button on each user message. *Connects to: RF04, RF08, RF10, RNF01, RNF09.*

**Screen 2 — Insertion Modal:** overlay with three ways to capture — raw text field, microphone (audio) and gallery/camera (photo) — with a transcription indicator. Every capture here creates a persisted entry, never a chat message. *Connects to: RF01, RF02.*

**Screen 3 — Side menu (sidebar):** navigation hub, session history, access to My Records / Action Plans / Settings, and a "Novo Chat" button that opens Screen 1 in its empty state. *Connects to: RF04 (via the "Novo Chat" button); the other items are pure navigation.*

**Screen 4 — My Records:** consolidated timeline, filters, manual tags (extension, section 2), export. *Connects to: RF07, RF06, RF05.*

**Screen 5 — Action Plans:** simple Kanban board (columns "A Fazer" / "Em Andamento" / "Concluído") with static example cards. *(Extension — section 2.)*

**Screen 6 — Settings and profile:** evolution dashboard, persona selector — "Analítico" / "Empático" / "Socrático" (extension, section 2; it would only change the system-prompt string of RF04), delete account. *Connects to: RF09, RNF05.*

---

The backend is already built and frozen. The API contract, `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, is the source of truth; this section is a reading of it oriented by screen and requirement. How to build the real URL of each operation: `docs/input/backend/README.md`.

Every endpoint returns errors in the standard contract of RNF09 — `{ code, message, retryable }` — and is protected by RLS in Supabase. Audio transcription (speech-to-text) runs on-device (Whisper) and never reaches the backend as an audio file.
