*(The amber "Action plans" subgraph marks the only screen with no backend calls — a product extension.)*

---

## 8. Data model (reference)

Main entities of the backend (Supabase / Postgres). Field names are reference suggestions, not mandatory character by character. **Where this table differs from the API contract (`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`), the contract prevails** (see section 6).

| Table | Main fields | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `users` | id, email, biometric_enabled, persona, created_at | RLS: a user accesses only their own row |
| `entries` | id, user_id, content, source (`manual`/`audio`/`photo`/`chat`), chat_message_id (nullable), embedding (vector, see 9), sync_status, created_at, updated_at | `embedding` generated in `POST /entries` via Voyage AI |
| `tags` | id, user_id, name | Extension — created manually by the user |
| `entry_tags` | entry_id, tag_id | N:N join table |
| `chat_sessions` | id, user_id, title, created_at | — |
| `chat_messages` | id, session_id, role (`user`/`assistant`), content, created_at | User messages show the RF10 button |
| `export_jobs` | id, user_id, status (`pending`/`processing`/`done`/`error`), period_start, period_end, file_url, created_at | Asynchronous — see 6.5 |

**RLS pattern (every table with `user_id`):** policy `auth.uid() = user_id`, no exceptions.

---

## 9. Technology stack

| Layer | Choice |
|---|---|
| Mobile app | Flutter, BLoC, Clean Architecture |
| Backend | Already built and frozen; consumed through its API |
| Infrastructure | Supabase (Postgres + pgvector + Storage + Auth + RLS) |
| Chat / vision / OCR / summary / insights / dashboard / PII | Claude Sonnet 5 (chat) + Claude Haiku 4.5 (the rest) — in the backend |
| Embeddings (RAG) | Voyage AI `voyage-4` — in the backend |
| Speech-to-text (audio transcription) | Whisper on-device (`whisper_ggml`); audio never reaches the backend |
| Error handling | `fpdart` (`Either<Failure, T>`) |
| Layer rule | RNF06 |
| Test coverage | RNF07 |

---

## 10. Configuration parameters

Fixed values — not to be reinterpreted.

| Parameter | Value | Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Background session timeout | 5 min | RF03 |
| Search debounce | 300 ms | RF06 |
| Proactive insight trigger | 5 messages OR 2 min of inactivity | RF08 |
| Dashboard rendering scenarios | 0 / 1 / > 30 entries | RF09 |
| Minimum test coverage (domain) | ≥ 80% | RNF07 |
| Local UI latency | < 100 ms | RNF01 |
| Loading-indicator threshold | > 300 ms | RNF01 |
| Network-error scenarios tested | 5 endpoints × 3 failures = 15 | RNF09 |

---

## 11. Error codes (RNF09)

Every endpoint returns `{ code, message, retryable }`. Minimum codes the app handles:

| Code | Situation | `retryable` |
|---|---|---|
| `AUTH_EXPIRED` | Session expired, re-authentication needed | no |
| `AUTH_INVALID` | Invalid credentials / biometrics | no |
| `NETWORK_TIMEOUT` | Request exceeded the time limit | yes |
| `NETWORK_OFFLINE` | No connection — action blocked (see RF04/RF06) | yes |
| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | Malformed request body | no |
| `PII_CHECK_FAILED` | PII check failed before persisting | yes |
| `EMBEDDING_FAILED` | Voyage AI unavailable / error | yes |
| `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT` | Claude did not respond in time (chat/insight/summary/dashboard) | yes |
| `NOT_FOUND` | Resource does not exist or does not belong to the user | no |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | Request limit exceeded | yes |

The complete, closed list of the backend's 13 codes, with HTTP statuses, is in `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md`.

---

## 12. Delivery order

Work is delivered in units, one per functional requirement, preceded by a foundation unit, in this order:

**F000 → RF03 → RF01 → RF02 → RF07 → RF06 → RF04 → RF10 → RF08 → RF05 → RF09**

- **F000 (foundation)** covers what no single requirement owns but all of them use: project scaffold, `design_tokens.dart`, HTTP client returning `Either`, login and sign-up (Screen 0.1a in the prototype), base navigation and expired-session handling.
- RF10 comes after RF01 and RF04; RF08 comes after RF04.

---

## 13. Technical constraints

**Fixed:**
- Flutter and Dart at the version pinned for the repository (fvm).
- State management: `flutter_bloc`.
- Clean Architecture, three layers per feature.
- Error handling: `fpdart`; repositories return `Either<Failure, T>`.
- Test doubles: `mocktail`.
- On-device speech-to-text: `whisper_ggml`.
- Visual tokens: `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` is the single source of colors, typography, spacing and radii.
- Platform: iOS, portrait only.
- Folder convention:

```
lib/
  core/
  features/
    <feature>/
      data/
      domain/
      presentation/
```

**Free (choose what fits):** routing, HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics package, chart package.

1	# Implementation Plan: P-RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
2	
3	**Branch**: `002-biometric-auth-vault` (spec directory only — no git branch exists; see spec header)
4	
5	**Date**: 2026-10-11 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)
6	
7	**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md`,
8	`docs/input/requirements.md` §1 (RF03), §10 (parameters), §13 (technical constraints), and
9	`.specify/memory/constitution.md`. Depends on F000 (`specs/001-foundation/`), already implemented.
10	
11	## Summary
12	
13	RF03 inserts a device-local Face ID / Touch ID / PIN barrier between F000's existing session
14	routing and any screen that shows user data. It adds exactly two new decision points to code F000
15	already ships — the splash screen's `authenticated` branch and the login/sign-up screen's success
16	branch — redirecting both from `AppRoutes.home` to a new `AppRoutes.vault` gate instead of adding a
17	parallel navigation scheme. That single screen (`VaultPage`) internally covers three of the
18	prototype's named states (Biometria, PIN inicial, PIN após falha) plus first-time PIN
19	creation, branching on whether a PIN is already configured on the device. A second, independent
20	mechanism — an app-lifecycle observer feeding a fixed 5-minute domain rule — re-pushes the same
21	screen over whatever is on screen when the app resumes from a long background period, without
22	disturbing that screen's state underneath (reusing F000's established `push`-only navigation
23	discipline, research.md R3). Authentication itself never leaves the device: no biometric data and
24	no PIN value are ever sent to the backend. The one network call this unit introduces —
25	persisting the `biometricEnabled` preference via the already-frozen `PATCH /account/settings`
26	— reuses F000's `ApiClient`/`Either<Failure, T>` path and is fire-and-forget by design (Clarifications).
27	
28	## Technical Context
29	
30	**Language/Version**: Dart 3.13.4 / Flutter 3.47.5 (stable), pinned via `.fvmrc` — unchanged from
31	F000, no new pin needed.
32	
33	**Primary Dependencies** (additions on top of F000's stack):
34	- `local_auth` — the official Flutter plugin for Face ID/Touch ID; see research.md R1.
35	- `crypto` — `sha256` hashing of the on-device PIN before it touches secure storage; see research.md R2.
36	- Reused unchanged from F000: `flutter_bloc`, `fpdart`, `dio` (via `ApiClient`), `get_it`,
37	  `flutter_secure_storage`, `equatable`, `go_router`; dev-only `mocktail`, `bloc_test`.
38	
39	**Storage**: `flutter_secure_storage`, extended with two new keys (PIN hash, local biometrics-
40	preference mirror) via a new `VaultSecureStorage` wrapper parallel to F000's `SecureTokenStorage` —

# Implementation Plan: P-RF03 — Biometric authentication vault

**Branch**: `002-biometric-auth-vault` (spec directory only — no git branch exists; see spec header)

**Date**: 2026-10-11 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)

**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/spec.md`,
`docs/input/requirements.md` §1 (RF03), §10 (parameters), §13 (technical constraints), and
`.specify/memory/constitution.md`. Depends on F000 (`specs/001-foundation/`), already implemented.

## Summary

RF03 inserts a device-local Face ID / Touch ID / PIN barrier between F000's existing session
routing and any screen that shows user data. It adds exactly two new decision points to code F000
already ships — the splash screen's `authenticated` branch and the login/sign-up screen's success
branch — redirecting both from `AppRoutes.home` to a new `AppRoutes.vault` gate instead of adding a
parallel navigation scheme. That single screen (`VaultPage`) internally covers three of the
prototype's named states (Biometria, PIN inicial, PIN após falha) plus first-time PIN
creation, branching on whether a PIN is already configured on the device. A second, independent
mechanism — an app-lifecycle observer feeding a fixed 5-minute domain rule — re-pushes the same
screen over whatever is on screen when the app resumes from a long background period, without
disturbing that screen's state underneath (reusing F000's established `push`-only navigation
discipline, research.md R3). Authentication itself never leaves the device: no biometric data and
no PIN value are ever sent to the backend. The one network call this unit introduces —
persisting the `biometricEnabled` preference via the already-frozen `PATCH /account/settings`
— reuses F000's `ApiClient`/`Either<Failure, T>` path and is fire-and-forget by design (Clarifications).

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: Dart 3.13.4 / Flutter 3.47.5 (stable), pinned via `.fvmrc` — unchanged from
F000, no new pin needed.

**Primary Dependencies** (additions on top of F000's stack):
- `local_auth` — the official Flutter plugin for Face ID/Touch ID; see research.md R1.
- `crypto` — `sha256` hashing of the on-device PIN before it touches secure storage; see research.md R2.

  `flutter_secure_storage`, `equatable`, `go_router`; dev-only `mocktail`, `bloc_test`.

**Storage**: `flutter_secure_storage`, extended with two new keys (PIN hash, local biometrics-
preference mirror) via a new `VaultSecureStorage` wrapper parallel to F000's `SecureTokenStorage` —
see data-model.md Device PIN / Biometrics Preference. No SQL/NoSQL local database is introduced.

**Testing**: `flutter_test` + `bloc_test` + `mocktail`, identical to F000; coverage via
`fvm flutter test --coverage`, same `lib/**/domain/**` lcov filter for the RNF07 gate. Device
biometric hardware cannot be exercised by `flutter_test` (no `local_auth` platform channel on the
test VM) — see quickstart.md for the manual iOS Simulator verification steps User Stories 1–2 need.

**Target Platform**: iOS, portrait only — unchanged. `local_auth` requires
`NSFaceIDUsageDescription` in `ios/Runner/Info.plist` (new, see research.md R1); no other native
project change.

**Project Type**: Same single Flutter mobile app; this unit adds one new `lib/features/vault/`
feature folder and touches two existing F000 files at their documented extension points (below).
No backend/server code, no change to `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`.

**Performance Goals**: RNF01 — the biometric prompt itself is OS-rendered (not timed against the
<100 ms/300 ms rule); the one network call this unit makes (`account-settings-update`) shows a
loading indicator only if it exceeds 300 ms, but per FR-014/Clarifications its outcome never blocks
navigation, so in practice no user-visible wait is introduced by this unit at all — PIN
creation/verification and the local biometric prompt are the sum of what stands between the user
and Home/Chat, and both are local.

- Authentication is validated entirely on-device (FR-002) — no biometric data or PIN value is ever

- The 5-minute background timeout is fixed, not user-configurable (FR-009, requirements.md §10).

- No backend/contract/config change (FR-018) — the only call made is to the already-existing

- Zero visual values hardcoded outside `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` (Principle IV/RNF08) — any

first-time setup as internal states, per prototype-extract.md's implementation note #1), 1 new

# Error taxonomy — 13 codes

Every endpoint returns errors as `{ code, message, retryable }`. The list below is closed: no other code exists.

| Code | HTTP | Retryable |
|---|---|---|
| `AUTH_EXPIRED` | 401 | no |
| `AUTH_INVALID` | 401 | no |
| `NETWORK_TIMEOUT` | 504 | yes |
| `NETWORK_OFFLINE` | _(no HTTP response — see note)_ | yes |
| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | no |
| `PII_CHECK_FAILED` | 502 | yes |
| `EMBEDDING_FAILED` | 502 | yes |
| `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT` | 504 | yes |
| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | no |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | yes |
| `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` | 400 | no |
| `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` | 413 | no |
| `OCR_NO_TEXT` | 400 | no |

**Two deliberate design choices (these never happen in this API):**
- **Never `403`** — a resource belonging to another user always answers `404 NOT_FOUND` (so its existence is not revealed).
- **Never `409`** — the idempotency of RF10 (re-sending the same chat message as an entry) always answers `200`; there is no "conflict" code.

**`NETWORK_OFFLINE` has no HTTP status:** it is the only code that never becomes an actual response — it represents a connection that ends without any response.

# Cerne backend — documentation package

The backend is already built and frozen. This package documents what the app needs to consume it. The backend source code is not part of it.

## Contents

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `api/openapi.yaml` | API contract of the 23 endpoints — the source of truth |
| `error-taxonomy.md` | The 13 error codes, with HTTP status and `retryable` |

| `known-bugs.md` | Known non-blocking backend defects, with workarounds |
| `fixtures/` | Test media (audio, images for OCR), the expected transcription of the audio, and the three seeded entries used by semantic search |

Credentials (project URL and keys) are not in this package: they are provided in the app's `.env`.

## Contract path → function

`api/openapi.yaml` has no router: each operation is served by its own Edge Function at `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<function>` (see `servers` and each operation's `x-cerne-function` in the YAML) — **never** directly at the REST path below. Path parameters are appended as the final URL segments, in the same order as they appear in the path; any literal segment after the last parameter (e.g., the `/retry` of `chat.messages.retry`) does not exist in the real URL.

182	
183	## 4. Special states that need extra care
184	
185	- **Expired session:** an overlay on the chat that keeps history and scroll position — the expired token must not discard the conversation state in memory before re-authentication. Re-authenticating goes back to the Biometria screen, not to a full form.
186	- **Offline:** blocks **sending new messages** (send icon disabled, explanatory banner), but **history stays visible and navigable**. The prototype does not show what happens to the insertion modal (text/audio/photo) when offline.
187	- **Asynchronous processing — audio transcription:** a loading state (spinner + frozen waveform) and two outcomes (success/error); the error always offers "Tentar novamente" and never loses the recorded audio.
188	- **Asynchronous processing — photo OCR:** same pattern as audio, with one extra exit on error: "Salvar só a foto", which saves the record even without extracted text.
189	- **Asynchronous processing — export:** two loading stages (preparing → generating the AI summary) before the result; on error, the raw data is always available for download — the failure is isolated to the AI narrative, never to the user's data.
190	- **Dashboard narrative unavailable:** the chart loads normally but the AI summary paragraph fails — distinct from "zero entries" (lack of data) and needs its own error message.
191	
192	---
193	
194	## 5. Implementation notes
195	
196	1. **"29 frames" vs. "32 states":** the prototype has 32 distinct navigable states, but the number of frames (29) suggests that some state families should be one screen with internal state, not separate routes (e.g., a single `ExportSheet` with a status enum instead of 5 routes). Consider this when designing navigation.
197	2. **Account deletion without a success screen:** both "Sair" and "Apagar tudo" return to the Biometria screen; there is no "account deleted" or "you signed out" screen.
198	3. **Login vs. sign-up:** the same screen toggled by a text link; the prototype shows no extra sign-up fields (e.g., password confirmation, name). Whether sign-up needs extra fields is a product decision not covered visually.
199	4. **Insertion modal when offline:** not represented.
200	5. **Switching tabs in the insertion modal:** opening the modal always resets every tab to `idle`/empty, but switching tabs *during* a modal session is not cleared automatically — the expected behavior (e.g., whether an ongoing recording is discarded on tab switch) is not defined by the prototype.
201	6. **Per-entry sync indicator:** the states "sincronizado / sincronizando / erro de sync" exist visually on the cards, but no explicit "retry sync" action is shown for the error state. The semantics of the badge are in `docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md`.
202	7. **Text search combined with filters:** the filter sheet and the text search are on the same screen, but the prototype does not show them acting together.
203

| Tela 1 — Offline | Blue-gray banner "Sem conexão — histórico disponível, novas mensagens bloqueadas"; send icon disabled. |
| Tela 1 — Sessão expirada | Light scrim over the chat (still readable), centered card with lock icon, title "Sessão expirada", text saying history and scroll position are kept, button "Entrar novamente". |
| Tela 3 — Menu lateral | Drawer: initials avatar and name; section "CONVERSAS" with past sessions (title + timestamp); items "Meus Registros", "Planos de Ação", "Configurações"; new-conversation action. |

### 2.3 Insertion modal (bottom sheet over Home/Chat; 9 states)
Common structure: "x" to close and a 3-tab bar (Texto / Áudio / Foto); the active tab has a filled dark-green background.

| State | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Texto | Multiline field, placeholder "Escreva livremente...", button "Salvar". |
| Áudio — Gravando | Red stop button, animated 12-bar waveform, monospace timer (e.g., "00:12"). |
| Áudio — Processando | Spinner in place of stop; frozen, faded waveform (opacity .35); text "Transcrevendo..."; label "00:42 de áudio". |
| Áudio — Transcrito | Editable transcribed text; original audio duration in mono; "Salvar" enabled. |
| Áudio — Erro | Red warning icon, "Não foi possível transcrever", outline button "Tentar novamente". |
| Foto — Captura | Two large buttons, "Câmera" and "Galeria". |
| Foto — Processando OCR | Photo thumbnail, spinner, "Reconhecendo texto...". |
| Foto — Reconhecido | Small thumbnail next to the extracted (editable) text; "Salvar". |
| Foto — Erro | Thumbnail kept, warning icon, "Não foi possível reconhecer o texto", button "Tentar novamente" and secondary text action "Salvar só a foto". |

### 2.4 Records
| State | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Tela 4 — Meus Registros (default) | Records grouped by date ("Hoje", "Ontem", dates); each card with a spine colored by origin, source icon, time, sync indicator (green "sincronizado" / ochre "sincronizando" / red "erro de sync"), text excerpt, category chips when present; header with back arrow, title, download icon; search bar "Buscar nos registros..." with a funnel button. |
| Tela 4 — Vazio | Large notebook icon, "Nenhum registro ainda", CTA "Criar primeiro registro". |
| Tela 4 — Filtros ativos | Removable chips under the search bar with the applied filters, link "Limpar filtros"; funnel button filled. |
| Tela 4 — Sheet de filtro | Groups "INTERVALO DE DATA" (Todo o período / Esta semana / Este mês, single choice), "CATEGORIA" (chips: trabalho, rotina, descanso, relações), "TIPO DE ENTRADA" (chips: manual, áudio, foto, chat); "Aplicar" and "Limpar". **Note:** the backend has no category filter (requirements, RF06); categories are the tags extension. |

### 2.5 Export (bottom sheet over Tela 4; 5 states)
| State | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Pendente | Spinner, "Preparando exportação...". |
| Processando | "Gerando resumo com IA...", progress bar. |
| Concluído | Green check, "Resumo pronto", buttons "Baixar PDF" (primary) and "Baixar dados brutos" (outline). |
| Erro | Red warning; text explaining that the AI narrative failed but the data remains available; only the button "Baixar dados brutos". |
| Período vazio | "Nenhum registro nesse período." and a suggestion to adjust the filter; no download button. |

All five have the link "Fechar" at the bottom. The mapping between these states and the backend job statuses is in `docs/input/backend/export-screen-states.md`.

### 2.6 Plans and settings
| State | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Tela 5 — Planos de Ação **[ext]** | Three horizontally scrolling columns — "A Fazer", "Em Andamento", "Concluído" — with counts and cards. |
| Tela 6 — Configurações — mais de 30 registros | "Sua evolução": 10-bar ochre chart + summary paragraph. |
| Tela 6 — Configurações — uma entrada | A single small bar and the text "Ainda é cedo pra ver um padrão — volte em alguns dias." |
| Tela 6 — Configurações — zero entradas | Light-gray chart icon in place of the chart and "Comece a registrar para ver sua evolução aqui"; no summary paragraph. |
| Tela 6 — Configurações — narrativa indisponível | Chart with data, but the AI summary paragraph failed — needs its own error message, not just missing text. |
| Tela 6 — Confirmar exclusão de conta | Centered dialog, red title "Apagar sua conta?", text on permanent, irreversible deletion; red button "Apagar tudo"; outline "Cancelar". |

Other elements of Configurações: avatar with editable name/e-mail (pencil becomes a check in edit mode — inline editing); persona cards "Como a IA responde" (Analítico, Empático, Socrático) **[ext]**; actions "Sair" and "Apagar conta" (red).

---

## 3. Visual system (tokens for `design_tokens.dart`)

The prototype has a **Design Tokens** panel, marked as the ground truth for `design_tokens.dart`. Its names and values are below.

### Colors
| Token | Hex | Use (as stated in the panel) |
|---|---|---|
| `colorPrimary` | `#1F3D34` | Buttons, app bar, wordmark |
| `colorPrimaryPressed` | `#16281F` | Pressed state |
| `colorOnPrimary` | `#F5F1E8` | Text on primary |
| `colorAccent` | `#C98A3E` | CTA, insight, saved bookmark |
| `colorOnAccent` | `#241C0D` | Text on accent |
| `colorSecondary` | `#7C8B6F` | Tags, chips, synchronizing |
| `colorSurfaceBg` | `#F2EFE7` | General background ("paper") |
| `colorSurfaceElevated` | `#FBF9F4` | Cards, bubbles, sheets |
| `colorBorder` | `#E1DACB` | Dividers, borders |
| `colorTextPrimary` | `#241F19` | Main text |
| `colorTextSecondary` | `#6B6255` | Secondary text |
| `colorError` | `#B3402A` | Errors, destructive action |
| `colorSuccess` | `#4C6B4F` | Synchronized, confirmations |
| `colorWarningSync` | `#C98A3E` | "Synchronizing" badge |
| `colorInfoOffline` | `#5C7A93` | Offline banner — single use |

Other colors that appear on specific screens but not in the panel: user chat bubble `#D9DFD3`; text on category chips `#3F4A38`.

### Typography
| Token | Font · weight · size/line-height | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `textDisplayLg` | Fraunces 600 · 32/38 | Splash wordmark |
| `textHeadlineMd` | Fraunces 600 · 24/30 | Section titles |
| `textTitleLg` | Karla 700 · 20/26 | App bar title |
| `textTitleSm` | Karla 700 · 16/22 | Subtitles |
| `textBodyLg` | Karla 400 · 16/24 | Bubbles, entries |
| `textBodyMd` | Karla 400 · 14/20 | Secondary text and descriptions |
| `textLabelMd` | Karla 500 · 13/18 | Button text, chips |
| `textMonoCaption` | IBM Plex Mono 500 · 12/16 · letter-spacing .2 | Technical metadata (timestamps, counters, status labels) |

### Spacing (4 dp grid)
`spacingXs` 4 · `spacingSm` 8 · `spacingMd` 16 · `spacingLg` 24 · `spacingXl` 32 · `spacing2xl` 48 (dp).

### Radii
`radiusSm` 8 dp (inputs, chips) · `radiusMd` 16 dp (cards, bubbles) · `radiusLg` 24 dp (sheets, modals) · `radiusFull` 999 dp (avatars, pills).

### Elevation
`elevation1` — `0 1px 3px rgba(36,31,25,.08)` (cards at rest) · `elevation2` — `0 4px 16px rgba(36,31,25,.14)` (sheets, modals).

### Icons
Phosphor library, Regular style, 24 dp: `list`, `plus`, `magnifying-glass`, `funnel`, `bookmark-simple`, `microphone`, `camera`, `gear`, `kanban`, `notebook`, `fingerprint`, `lightbulb` (and others used on specific screens: `check`, `warning-circle`, `wifi-slash`, `circle-notch`, `caret-left`, `download-simple`, `pencil-simple`, `x`, `stop`, `image`, `check-circle`, `chart-line-up`, `backspace`, `lock-key`, `paper-plane-tilt`, `chat-circle-text`).

### Spine (colored bar on the left of a card) — 3 contexts
1. Proactive insight in the chat — ochre.
2. Entry origin in "Meus Registros" — color by type: manual = dark green, audio = olive green, photo = gray, chat = ochre.
3. Kanban column in "Planos de Ação" — color by column **[ext]**.

### Micro-animations and transitions
- `scrimIn` (0.18 s ease-out): fade of the darkened background when any overlay opens.
- `sheetUp` (0.2 s ease-out): bottom sheets (insertion modal, filter, export) rise from the bottom of the screen.
- Continuous spinner (`spin`, 1 s linear infinite) in every loading state.
- Text streaming: the AI response is revealed progressively, with a blinking cursor at the end while it is "typing".
- PIN: after the 4th digit, a 350 ms pause before navigating.

---

## 4. Special states that need extra care

- **Expired session:** an overlay on the chat that keeps history and scroll position — the expired token must not discard the conversation state in memory before re-authentication. Re-authenticating goes back to the Biometria screen, not to a full form.
- **Offline:** blocks **sending new messages** (send icon disabled, explanatory banner), but **history stays visible and navigable**. The prototype does not show what happens to the insertion modal (text/audio/photo) when offline.
- **Asynchronous processing — audio transcription:** a loading state (spinner + frozen waveform) and two outcomes (success/error); the error always offers "Tentar novamente" and never loses the recorded audio.
- **Asynchronous processing — photo OCR:** same pattern as audio, with one extra exit on error: "Salvar só a foto", which saves the record even without extracted text.
- **Asynchronous processing — export:** two loading stages (preparing → generating the AI summary) before the result; on error, the raw data is always available for download — the failure is isolated to the AI narrative, never to the user's data.
- **Dashboard narrative unavailable:** the chart loads normally but the AI summary paragraph fails — distinct from "zero entries" (lack of data) and needs its own error message.

---

## 5. Implementation notes

1. **"29 frames" vs. "32 states":** the prototype has 32 distinct navigable states, but the number of frames (29) suggests that some state families should be one screen with internal state, not separate routes (e.g., a single `ExportSheet` with a status enum instead of 5 routes). Consider this when designing navigation.
2. **Account deletion without a success screen:** both "Sair" and "Apagar tudo" return to the Biometria screen; there is no "account deleted" or "you signed out" screen.
3. **Login vs. sign-up:** the same screen toggled by a text link; the prototype shows no extra sign-up fields (e.g., password confirmation, name). Whether sign-up needs extra fields is a product decision not covered visually.
4. **Insertion modal when offline:** not represented.
5. **Switching tabs in the insertion modal:** opening the modal always resets every tab to `idle`/empty, but switching tabs *during* a modal session is not cleared automatically — the expected behavior (e.g., whether an ongoing recording is discarded on tab switch) is not defined by the prototype.
6. **Per-entry sync indicator:** the states "sincronizado / sincronizando / erro de sync" exist visually on the cards, but no explicit "retry sync" action is shown for the error state. The semantics of the badge are in `docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md`.
7. **Text search combined with filters:** the filter sheet and the text search are on the same screen, but the prototype does not show them acting together.

---

## 6. Component library

| Component | Where it appears | Variations |
|---|---|---|
| Primary button | Auth, modals, sheets, confirmations | normal (`#1F3D34`) · pressed (`#16281F`, darker) · disabled (`#E1DACB` background, `#6B6255` text) |
| Secondary button (outline) | "Tentar novamente", "Cancelar", "Baixar dados brutos" | `#1F3D34` outline, no fill |
| Text button (ghost) | Mode-toggle links, "Fechar", "Limpar" | no background, `#1F3D34` or `#6B6255` depending on context |
| Text field | Login, Texto tab, name editing | empty · focused (1.5px `#1F3D34` border) · error (`#B3402A` border) |
| Chat bubble | Home/Chat | user (light green, straight bottom-right corner) · AI (ivory with shadow, straight bottom-left corner) · streaming (pulsing cursor at the end of the text) |
| Insight card | Home/Chat | ochre spine, mono label "INSIGHT", dismiss button |
| Bookmark button (RF10) | User messages in the chat | idle (outline) · saving (spinner) · saved (ochre check) · error (red warning) |
| Send-error banner | Home/Chat | "Não foi possível enviar — toque para tentar novamente"; background `rgba(179,64,42,.08)`, warning icon, red text |
| Offline banner | Home/Chat | blue-gray background `#5C7A93`, `ph-wifi-slash` icon, light text |
| Sync badge | Record cards (Tela 4) | synced (green dot) · synchronizing (ochre dot) · sync error (red dot) |
| Filter chip | Filter sheet, active filters | single choice (date) · multiple choice (category, type) · removable with "x" (active filters) |
| Record card | Tela 4 | spine colored by origin (manual = dark green, audio = olive green, photo = gray, chat = ochre) |
| Kanban card **[ext]** | Planos de Ação | spine by column (to do / in progress / done) |
| Initials avatar | Side menu, Configurações | dark green circle, 1–2 uppercase initials, two sizes (40px in the menu, 52px in Configurações) |
| AI persona card **[ext]** | Configurações | not selected (thin border) · selected (thick `#1F3D34` border + check icon) |
| Bar chart (dashboard) | Configurações | populated (10 bars) · one bar · empty (placeholder icon) |
| Export status card | Tela 4 (bottom sheet) | pending · processing · done · error · empty |
| Confirmation dialog | Sessão expirada, Confirmar exclusão | background scrim + centered card; neutral title (session) or red title (destructive deletion) |
| PIN keypad | Tela 0.1b/c | digits 0–9 + backspace; progress dots above |
| Tab bar | Insertion modal | 3 tabs (Texto/Áudio/Foto), active tab with filled background |
| Audio waveform | Insertion modal, Áudio tab | active/animated (recording) · frozen and faded (processing) |
| Skeleton | Any content loaded over the network | shown for calls longer than 300 ms (RNF01) |

1	# Research: P-RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
2	
3	F000's research.md explicitly left "biometrics" open for "the units that need them (RF03, RF09)."
4	This file resolves that, plus every other free choice and silent spot this unit's spec surfaces.
5	
6	## R1 — Biometrics package
7	
8	- **Decision**: `local_auth` (the official `flutter.dev`-maintained plugin), called with
9	  `authenticate(biometricOnly: true)`.
10	- **Rationale**: FR-004 requires that a failed/unavailable biometric attempt fall through to the
11	  app's **own** 4-digit PIN, never to the iOS device passcode. `local_auth`'s `biometricOnly: true`
12	  option is honored on iOS (it pins the underlying `LAPolicy` to
13	  `LAPolicyDeviceOwnerAuthenticationWithBiometrics`, which has no device-passcode fallback built
14	  in) — exactly the primitive FR-004 needs. `local_auth` also exposes `canCheckBiometrics` and
15	  `isDeviceSupported()` ahead of calling `authenticate`, which FR-003 and the Edge Cases ("no
16	  hardware," "nothing enrolled," "disabled at the OS level") need to distinguish from an in-progress
17	  failed attempt. It is the only Flutter-ecosystem plugin maintained by the Flutter team itself for
18	  this exact purpose, consistent with picking boring, well-supported dependencies for a stack the
19	  constitution otherwise keeps deliberately small.
20	- **Alternatives considered**: Rolling a native iOS `LAContext` call through a hand-written
21	  platform channel — rejected, `local_auth` already wraps exactly this with no extra capability
22	  gained from going lower-level, for meaningfully more code to own and test. Third-party biometrics
23	  wrappers (e.g. ones that bundle PIN-entry UI too) — rejected, this unit already owns PIN entry per
24	  FR-005/the prototype's exact keypad spec, and a bundled UI would fight Principle IV (design-token
25	  fidelity) rather than help.
26	- **Native project note**: `local_auth`'s iOS backend requires `NSFaceIDUsageDescription` in
27	  `ios/Runner/Info.plist` (a one-line string the App Store requires before Face ID can even be
28	  attempted) — the only native project file this unit touches, and a hard requirement of the
29	  package rather than a product decision. No Android work exists in this project (iOS-only,
30	  Principle II).
31	
32	## R2 — PIN storage
33	
34	- **Decision**: Store `sha256(pin)` (hex string) via a new `VaultSecureStorage` key, never the raw
35	  4-digit value. Verification re-hashes the entered PIN and compares digests.
36	- **Rationale**: `flutter_secure_storage` is already Keychain-backed (R5 of F000's research.md),
37	  so storing the raw PIN would not be *readable* in plaintext at rest either — but hashing is the
38	  standard defense-in-depth for any credential-shaped value regardless of the storage layer
39	  underneath, and it is a one-function addition (`crypto`'s `sha256`) with no behavioral
40	  downside: the PIN is never displayed back to the user, so there is no legitimate need to ever
41	  recover the raw value, only to compare it. This mirrors how the backend itself never stores or
42	  sees passwords in the clear.
43	- **Alternatives considered**: Storing the raw PIN string — rejected as an avoidable weakening for
44	  zero functional gain. A salted hash (per-install random salt, also stored) — rejected as
45	  over-engineering: the threat a salt defends against is an attacker who has compromised *many*
46	  users' hash stores at once and wants to precompute one rainbow table across all of them; here,
47	  each hash lives alone inside that one device's own encrypted Keychain entry for that one user, so
48	  a salt adds code and a second stored value without changing what an attacker who already has
49	  Keychain access could do.
50	
51	## R3 — Where the 5-minute relock timer lives
52	
53	- **Decision**: One root-level `StatefulWidget` (`VaultLifecycleObserver`), installed once in
54	  `main.dart`'s `CerneApp.builder` (the same spot F000 installs the session-expired
55	  `BlocListener`), implementing `WidgetsBindingObserver`. On `AppLifecycleState.paused` it calls
56	  into the long-lived `VaultRepository` singleton to record "now"; on `.resumed` it asks a pure
57	  domain usecase (`EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase`) whether that gap was ≥ 5 minutes, and if so
58	  pushes `VaultPage(mode: relock)` via the existing `rootNavigatorKey` — the same root navigator
59	  `session_expired_overlay.dart` already pushes onto.
60	- **Rationale**: FR-007/FR-008/FR-010 and User Story 1's background-resume scenarios are a
61	  cross-cutting concern that has nothing to do with *which* screen happens to be on top — exactly
62	  the shape F000's own `SessionBloc` + root `BlocListener` pattern was built for (research.md R3
63	  there). Reusing `rootNavigatorKey` and plain `push` (never `go`/replace) is what makes "the screen
64	  underneath keeps its exact state" (FR-010) true by construction, not by a second bespoke
65	  mechanism — the same guarantee `session_expired_overlay.dart` already relies on for its own
66	  overlay.
67	- **Why not persist the last-unlock timestamp to disk**: the only case that would matter for is the
68	  OS killing the process while backgrounded — but that case is *already* handled for free: a killed
69	  process means the next launch is a cold launch, which always re-enters `SplashPage` → the
70	  `AppRoutes.vault` gatekeeper path regardless of elapsed time (Edge Cases: "the next launch is
71	  treated as a cold launch and always shows the vault"). An in-memory timestamp on a singleton
72	  repository is therefore sufficient; persisting it would add a disk write on every background
73	  transition for a case that can't be reached.
74	- **Alternatives considered**: A second root-level `Bloc` dedicated to lock state — rejected as an
75	  unnecessary extra moving part; the logic needed (record a timestamp, compare it, decide whether
76	  to push one specific, already-existing route) does not need its own event/state machine distinct
77	  from the domain usecase plus a thin observer widget. A `Timer.periodic` ticking down from 5
78	  minutes while foregrounded — rejected: FR-007/FR-008 only care about elapsed *background* time,
79	  not foreground idle time (that is RF08's unrelated 2-minute inactivity trigger), so a running
80	  foreground timer would be solving a problem this requirement doesn't have.
81	
82	## R4 — The single-screen vault (gatekeeper vs. relock, setup vs. unlock)
83	
84	- **Decision**: One route (`AppRoutes.vault`), one page (`VaultPage`), one screen-scoped
85	  `VaultBloc`, branching internally on two independent axes: (a) **mode** — `gatekeeper` (reached
86	  from `SplashPage` or `LoginSignupPage`, resolves by going to `AppRoutes.home` on success) vs.
87	  `relock` (reached from `VaultLifecycleObserver`, resolves by popping back to the preserved screen
88	  underneath); (b) **entry decision** — `pinSetupRequired` vs. `locked(biometricFirst | pinOnly)`,
89	  computed once by `DetermineVaultEntryUseCase` when the page opens.
90	- **Rationale**: prototype-extract.md's own implementation note #1 flags that "32 states" collapse
91	  into fewer real screens with internal state, naming this exact family (Biometria / PIN inicial /
92	  PIN após falha) as a candidate. The spec's own Assumptions go further and fold first-time PIN
93	  creation into the same keypad component rather than inventing a fourth undocumented screen. A
94	  `relock` entry can never need the `pinSetupRequired` branch (a relock is only ever triggered after

100	  widget and its 350 ms-after-4th-digit transition behavior four times instead of once.
101

103	
104	- **Decision**: `Either<Failure, T>` is used only where this unit actually talks to the network —
105	  `BiometricsPreferenceRepository`. `VaultRepository` (PIN verification, biometric hardware
106	  queries, the in-memory relock timestamp) returns plain `bool`/`DateTime?`/domain-enum values, not
107	  `Either<Failure, T>`.
108	- **Rationale**: RNF09's `Failure` hierarchy (`core/network/failure.dart`) is explicitly the
109	  backend's own closed 13-code taxonomy (F000 research.md R6) — `AUTH_EXPIRED`,
110	  `NETWORK_TIMEOUT`, and so on are all things *a server response* can say. A missing fingerprint
111	  sensor or a wrong PIN digest is not a server outcome and has no corresponding code; forcing it
112	  through `Either<Failure, T>` would mean either inventing fake codes for purely local conditions
113	  (polluting a taxonomy the spec calls "closed") or always returning a code that doesn't really fit.
114	  Constitution Principle I directs implementers to make the reasonable call where the inputs are
115	  silent, and RNF09's own wording ("every repository") is about the network-error-handling pattern
116	  the requirement is named for — not a blanket ban on any repository ever returning something else
117	  for a condition that isn't a network failure.
118	- **Alternatives considered**: Modeling PIN/biometric outcomes as `Either<Failure, T>` with new

120	  taxonomy with codes the backend's `error-taxonomy.md` doesn't define and that no later unit's
121	  network code would ever need to pattern-match on, diluting the one place (`failure.dart`) F000
122	  deliberately kept scoped to the backend's own 13 codes (F000 research.md R6).
123	
124	## R6 — `biometricEnabled` write semantics (building on the Clarifications session)
125	
126	- **Decision**: `SaveBiometricsPreferenceUseCase` writes the local mirror flag
127	  (`VaultRepository.setBiometricPreferenceLocally`) synchronously, then fires the
128	  `BiometricsPreferenceRepository.save()` network call and discards its `Either` result — no retry
129	  loop, no error banner, no blocking of the PIN-setup-complete transition to Home/Chat.
130	- **Rationale**: This is the literal mechanics of the Clarifications session's resolution
131	  ("proceed locally and retry in the background... first-time setup does not block on this write
132	  succeeding") plus the matching Edge Case ("the write is not retried synchronously as part of the
133	  setup flow"). The *local* mirror is what every later vault unlock actually reads to decide
134	  biometric-first vs. PIN-only (FR-003) — the backend's copy of `biometricEnabled` is a durable
135	  record for whichever later unit (RF09's Settings screen) needs to display or change it, not the
136	  value this unit's own unlock logic depends on at runtime.
137	- **What "retry through the existing failure-handling path" means here**: concretely, nothing new
138	  is built for it in this unit — the failed write simply isn't retried by RF03 at all. If the user
139	  later opens Settings (RF09) and that screen reads the account record, any mismatch between the
140	  local mirror and the stale backend value is that unit's reconciliation problem, not this one's;
141	  RF03 does not introduce a background sync queue, which would be speculative machinery for a case
142	  the spec explicitly says not to block on.
143	- **Alternatives considered**: A `WorkManager`/background-retry-queue style mechanism — rejected as
144	  out of proportion to a single boolean field and explicitly not what the Clarifications answer
145	  asked for.
146	
147	## R7 — New design tokens this unit needs
148	
149	- **Decision**: Add exactly one new token, `sizeKeypadTapTarget` (72 dp — a 4×-grid value,
150	  consistent with the existing `spacing*` scale, sized for a comfortable thumb target per the

153	  F000.
154	- **Rationale**: prototype-extract.md §3 does not give the PIN keypad an explicit pixel size (only
155	  "3×4 numeric keypad with backspace"), so this is the one silent spot Principle I's "reasonable
156	  technical decision" applies to visually — and per Principle IV it must still be a named constant
157	  in `design_tokens.dart`, not an inline literal in `pin_keypad.dart`.
158	- **Icons**: continuing F000's already-established precedent of using Flutter's built-in
159	  `Icons.*` (Material) rather than the prototype's specified Phosphor set (F000 used `Icons.send`,
160	  `Icons.lock` — see `home_chat_shell_page.dart`, `session_expired_overlay.dart`) — this unit uses
161	  `Icons.fingerprint` (Biometria's fingerprint circle), `Icons.backspace` (keypad backspace), and
162	  `Icons.lock_outline` (PIN screen header), introducing no new icon package.

- **Rationale**: This is the literal mechanics of the Clarifications session's resolution
  ("proceed locally and retry in the background... first-time setup does not block on this write
  succeeding") plus the matching Edge Case ("the write is not retried synchronously as part of the
  setup flow"). The *local* mirror is what every later vault unlock actually reads to decide
  biometric-first vs. PIN-only (FR-003) — the backend's copy of `biometricEnabled` is a durable
  record for whichever later unit (RF09's Settings screen) needs to display or change it, not the
  value this unit's own unlock logic depends on at runtime.
- **What "retry through the existing failure-handling path" means here**: concretely, nothing new
  is built for it in this unit — the failed write simply isn't retried by RF03 at all. If the user
  later opens Settings (RF09) and that screen reads the account record, any mismatch between the
  local mirror and the stale backend value is that unit's reconciliation problem, not this one's;
  RF03 does not introduce a background sync queue, which would be speculative machinery for a case
  the spec explicitly says not to block on.
- **Alternatives considered**: A `WorkManager`/background-retry-queue style mechanism — rejected as
  out of proportion to a single boolean field and explicitly not what the Clarifications answer
  asked for.

## R7 — New design tokens this unit needs

- **Decision**: Add exactly one new token, `sizeKeypadTapTarget` (72 dp — a 4×-grid value,
  consistent with the existing `spacing*` scale, sized for a comfortable thumb target per the
  prototype's 390×844 frame), to `design_tokens.dart`. Everything else the vault screens need
  (error-band red, primary buttons, body/title text styles, spacing, radii) already exists from
  F000.
- **Rationale**: prototype-extract.md §3 does not give the PIN keypad an explicit pixel size (only
  "3×4 numeric keypad with backspace"), so this is the one silent spot Principle I's "reasonable
  technical decision" applies to visually — and per Principle IV it must still be a named constant
  in `design_tokens.dart`, not an inline literal in `pin_keypad.dart`.
- **Icons**: continuing F000's already-established precedent of using Flutter's built-in
  `Icons.*` (Material) rather than the prototype's specified Phosphor set (F000 used `Icons.send`,
  `Icons.lock` — see `home_chat_shell_page.dart`, `session_expired_overlay.dart`) — this unit uses
  `Icons.fingerprint` (Biometria's fingerprint circle), `Icons.backspace` (keypad backspace), and
  `Icons.lock_outline` (PIN screen header), introducing no new icon package.

## Official Image Picker Plugin

The image_picker plugin is a Flutter package for picking images from the image library and taking new pictures with the camera. It supports iOS 13+ and multiple platforms including Android, Linux, macOS, Web, and Windows.

### iOS Setup

Starting with version 0.8.1, the iOS implementation uses PHPicker to pick images on iOS 14 or higher. For iOS, you need to add NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription to your Info.plist file to describe why your app needs permission for the photo library.

### Usage Example

The plugin provides methods like `pickImage(source: ImageSource.gallery)` to pick an image from the gallery and `pickImage(source: ImageSource.camera)` to capture a photo. Starting with version 0.8.2, new methods return XFile instances rather than the plugin's own PickedFile instances.

## Alternative Packages

There are several other image picker packages available on pub.dev:
- **image_picker_gallery_camera** - Allows picking from both camera and gallery with configurable options
- **my_image_picker** - Features automatic permission handling
- **image_picker_widget** - Integrates image_picker with a simple Flutter widget and image cropping

All of these packages require similar iOS permission configurations through the Info.plist file.

Based on the search results, here's information about the whisper_ggml Flutter pub.dev package API usage:

## Overview

Whisper GGML is an on-device speech-to-text solution for Flutter, powered by whisper.cpp v1.9.1. It can transcribe audio files or live speech with no server or API keys required.

## API Usage

### Basic Usage (File Transcription)

To transcribe an audio file, import the package and create a WhisperController, then call the transcribe method with a model, audio path, and language specification. Here's the basic pattern:

```dart
import 'package:whisper_ggml/whisper_ggml.dart';

final controller = WhisperController();
final result = await controller.transcribe(
  model: WhisperModel.tiny,
  audioPath: '/path/to/audio.wav',
  lang: 'en',
);
```

### Model Loading

The model loads once per session and an adaptive energy gate keeps silence from producing hallucinated text. Models download once and are cached, or can be shipped in your app's assets for fully offline use.

### Additional Features

You can pass withSegments: true to get per-segment timestamps, and splitOnWord: true for one segment per word instead of per phrase. In newer versions, you can pass onProgress: (percent) => ... to receive transcription progress as a 0–100 percentage while inference runs.

### Supported Platforms

The package supports Android (API 21+), iOS (15.6+), macOS (10.15+), Windows 10 (x64), and Linux x64.

The `onAmplitudeChanged` method with a specified duration interval can be used to listen to amplitude changes, and the result is processed in a listener that updates state. Here's an example pattern from the package documentation:

6	and no new local database (just two new secure-storage keys alongside F000's four).

11	(User Stories 1–2). Never transmitted to, or validated by, the backend (FR-002).

13	| Field | Type | Notes |
14	|---|---|---|
15	| `pinHash` | `String` (hex, sha256) | Written by `VaultSecureStorage`; see research.md R2 for why the raw digit string is never the thing stored. |
16

18	compared (FR-005). Confirmation during setup is a pure string-equality check between two freshly
19	entered 4-digit values — the first one is held only in memory (`VaultState`) between entry and
20	confirmation, never written to storage until it matches (FR-012: "without the mismatched PIN being
21	saved").

23	## Vault Lock State
24	
25	Whether the current app process currently requires authentication before showing data, and when it
26	was last satisfied — the input to the 5-minute background-resume rule (FR-007–FR-010).
27	
28	| Field | Type | Notes |
29	|---|---|---|
30	| `lastUnlockedAt` | `DateTime?` | In-memory only, held by the `VaultRepository` singleton (one instance for the app's lifetime via `get_it`'s `registerLazySingleton`). `null` until the first successful unlock this process. Never persisted to disk — see research.md R3 for why a killed/relaunched process doesn't need this to survive. |
31	| `backgroundedAt` | `DateTime?` | Set by `VaultLifecycleObserver` on `AppLifecycleState.paused`; read and cleared on the matching `.resumed`. In-memory only, same lifetime as `lastUnlockedAt`. |
32	
33	**Derived decision — `VaultEntryMode`** (domain enum/sealed type, computed by
34	`DetermineVaultEntryUseCase` every time `VaultPage` opens):
35	
36	```
37	pinSetupRequired                      # hasPinConfigured() == false
38	unlockBiometricFirst                  # PIN exists AND biometric capability == available
39	                                       #   AND the local biometrics-preference mirror == true
40	unlockPinOnly                         # PIN exists AND (no biometric capability OR preference == false)
41	```
42	
43	**State transitions**:
44	
45	```
46	[SplashPage, SessionStatusAuthenticated]  or  [LoginSignupPage, AuthStatus.authenticated (non-reauth)]
47	  context.push(AppRoutes.vault)   # mode: gatekeeper
48	      VaultPage opens -> DetermineVaultEntryUseCase()
49	          pinSetupRequired      -> show "Digite seu PIN" (new) -> confirm -> [optional] offer biometrics
50	                                     -> on complete: markUnlocked() -> context.go(AppRoutes.home)     (Story 3)
51	          unlockBiometricFirst  -> auto-trigger local_auth prompt
52	              success                     -> markUnlocked() -> context.go(AppRoutes.home)   (Story 1)
53	              failed/cancelled/notAvailable -> show "Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN" + PIN keypad (Story 2;
54	                                                notAvailable routed identically — e.g. biometric lockout mid-session)
55	                  correct PIN      -> markUnlocked() -> context.go(AppRoutes.home)
56	                  incorrect PIN    -> clear digits, keep error banner, no lockout, retry allowed (Story 2, Edge Cases)
57	          unlockPinOnly          -> show PIN keypad directly, no biometric prompt attempted (Edge Cases: no hardware/not enrolled/OS-disabled)
58	      at any point: "usar e-mail e senha" -> context.push(AppRoutes.login)          (Story 4)
59

61	  rootNavigatorKey.push(VaultPage)   # mode: relock — pushed OVER whatever screen is current
62	      VaultPage opens -> DetermineVaultEntryUseCase()   # always unlockBiometricFirst or unlockPinOnly — PIN already exists
63	          success (biometric or PIN)  -> markUnlocked() -> Navigator.pop()   # reveals the preserved screen underneath, state untouched
64	
65	[VaultLifecycleObserver, AppLifecycleState.resumed, EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase() == false]
66	  no-op — screen underneath was never covered, no re-authentication required   (FR-008)
67	```
68	
69	**Fixed rule** (`EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase`, FR-009):
70	
71	```dart
72	bool call({required DateTime? backgroundedAt, required DateTime resumedAt}) {
73	  if (backgroundedAt == null) return false;
74	  return resumedAt.difference(backgroundedAt) >= const Duration(minutes: 5);
75	}
76	```
77	
78	A pure function of two timestamps and one constant — no settings read, no parameter — is itself
79	the mechanism by which FR-009's "fixed value, not configurable by the user" is enforced.
80	
81	## Biometrics Preference
82	
83	An account-level flag indicating whether Face ID/Touch ID is the user's chosen unlock method —
84	read locally at every vault entry to decide `unlockBiometricFirst` vs. `unlockPinOnly`, and mirrored
85	to the backend for durability/future display (RF09's Settings screen), per FR-013.
86	
87	| Field | Type | Notes |
88	|---|---|---|
89	| `biometricPreferenceLocal` | `bool` | Written to `VaultSecureStorage` during first-time PIN setup (Story 3, scenario 4) if the user opts in; this is the value `DetermineVaultEntryUseCase` actually reads at runtime — never the backend's copy (research.md R6). Defaults to `false` until set. |
90	| `biometricEnabled` (remote) | `bool` | The backend's `users.biometric_enabled` field (requirements.md §8), read/written only through `PATCH /account/settings` → `account-settings-update`. This unit only ever **writes** it (fire-and-forget, FR-014); it never reads it back. |
91	
92	**Write path** (`SaveBiometricsPreferenceUseCase`, FR-013/FR-014):
93	
94	```
95	1. VaultRepository.setBiometricPreferenceLocally(enabled)        # synchronous, always succeeds (local write)
96	2. BiometricsPreferenceRepository.save(enabled)                  # await, discard Either<Failure, T> result
97	3. proceed to Home/Chat regardless of step 2's outcome            # Clarifications; Edge Cases
98	```
99	
100	## Backend Failure (reused, not redefined)
101	
102	`BiometricsPreferenceRepository.save()` is the only network call this unit makes; it returns
103	`Either<Failure, T>` using F000's existing `core/network/failure.dart` hierarchy unchanged (no new
104	`Failure` subtype — research.md R5). The three scenarios covered by this unit's own tests, toward
105	RNF09's 15-scenario total:
106	
107	| Scenario | Expected `Failure` | `retryable` |
108	|---|---|---|
109	| Request exceeds the timeout | `NetworkTimeoutFailure` | yes |
110	| No connection at all | `NetworkOfflineFailure` | yes |
111	| Malformed response body | `ValidationFailure` | no |
112	
113	None of these three block the PIN-setup-complete transition (R6) — they are observed only by this
114	unit's own `mocktail` tests of `BiometricsPreferenceRepositoryImpl`, never surfaced to the user.
115	
116	## Biometric Capability (domain enum, no `local_auth` type crosses into `domain/`)
117	
118	```
119	available        # canCheckBiometrics && isDeviceSupported && getAvailableBiometrics().isNotEmpty
120	noHardware        # isDeviceSupported == false
121	notEnrolled        # hardware present, nothing enrolled at the OS level
122	osDisabled        # was available in a previous session, no longer (Edge Cases: OS-level disable between sessions)
123	```
124	
125	`LocalAuthBiometricDataSource` (data layer) is the only place that imports `local_auth`'s own
126	types (`LocalAuthentication`, `AuthenticationOptions`, `BiometricType`); `VaultRepositoryImpl` maps
127	its result into this enum before it ever reaches `domain/` or `presentation/` (RNF06).

132	  decides `go(home)` vs. `pop()` on success (data-model.md State transitions above). Passed as a

138	  reset to empty after every failed attempt (Edge Cases: "the entered digits are cleared").
139

141

143	(`colorPrimary`, `colorOnPrimary`, `colorError`, `colorSurfaceBg`, `textHeadlineMd`, `textBodyMd`,
144	`textTitleSm`, `spacing*`, `radius*`). Three values are new, per research.md R7 and the "Tela 0.1"
145	fidelity fix:

3	How to validate this unit end-to-end once implemented, mapped to spec.md's four user stories. This

20	
21	```bash
22	fvm flutter analyze                                    # RNF06 import-shape lint (always_use_package_imports)
23	fvm flutter test --coverage
24	# RNF07 gate — same lcov filter F000 uses, now including lib/features/vault/domain
25	lcov --extract coverage/lcov.info 'lib/**/domain/**' -o coverage/domain.info
26	genhtml coverage/domain.info -o coverage/domain-html   # inspect % manually, or script a threshold check
27	```
28	
29	Key domain tests this unit's coverage depends on (contracts/vault-repository.md,
30	contracts/vault-lifecycle.md):
31	- `EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase`: exact-boundary cases (4:59 → false, 5:00 → true), `null`
32	  `backgroundedAt` → false.
33	- `DetermineVaultEntryUseCase`: all four input combinations (no PIN; PIN + biometric available +
34	  preferred; PIN + biometric available + not preferred; PIN + biometric unavailable).
35	- `VerifyPinUseCase`/`SavePinUseCase` against a fake `VaultRepository`.
36	- `BiometricsPreferenceRepositoryImpl`: the 3 failure scenarios in
37	  contracts/biometrics-preference-repository.md.
38	
39	## Manual verification (device/Simulator — `local_auth` has no platform channel under `flutter_test`)
40	
41	The iOS Simulator supports Face ID without real hardware: **Features → Face ID → Enrolled**, then
42	**Features → Face ID → Matching Face** / **Non-matching Face** to simulate a pass/fail scan on
43	demand.
44	
45	### Story 1 — Unlock with Face ID/Touch ID (P1)
46	
47	1. Enroll Face ID in the Simulator; complete sign-up once (Story 3 flow below) with the biometric
48	   opt-in accepted.
49	2. Force-quit and relaunch the app (cold launch).
50	3. **Expect**: Splash → vault screen with the fingerprint prompt, before any Home/Chat content
51	   renders. **Features → Face ID → Matching Face** → app proceeds straight to Home/Chat.
52	4. Background the app (Simulator: Cmd+Shift+H or Device → Home), wait 5+ minutes (or temporarily
53	   lower the constant in a local-only debug build to verify the mechanism faster, then revert),
54	   bring it back. **Expect**: vault screen re-appears over Home/Chat; matching Face ID again
55	   reveals Home/Chat exactly as left (scroll position, any in-progress state).
56	5. Repeat the same background/resume but under 5 minutes. **Expect**: no vault screen, Home/Chat
57	   is immediately interactive.
58	
59	### Story 2 — Biometric failure falls back to PIN (P1)
60	
61	1. From the vault screen's fingerprint prompt, **Features → Face ID → Non-matching Face**.
62	2. **Expect**: PIN keypad appears immediately with "Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN".
63	3. Enter the correct 4-digit PIN. **Expect**: unlocks normally.
64	4. Repeat; enter an incorrect PIN. **Expect**: digits clear, error state remains, no limit —
65	   retry with the correct PIN still works afterward.
66	
67	### Story 3 — First-time PIN setup (P2)
68	
69	1. Delete the app (or clear its Keychain data) to guarantee no PIN/session exists; launch fresh.
70	2. Sign up with a new email. **Expect**: immediately after signup succeeds, the create-PIN screen
71	   appears (not Home/Chat) — 4 progress dots, 3×4 keypad.
72	3. Enter 4 digits; **expect** the confirmation step. Enter a *different* 4 digits. **Expect**: clear
73	   mismatch message, returned to entering a new PIN, nothing saved yet.
74	4. Enter and confirm matching PINs. If the Simulator has Face ID enrolled, **expect** a biometrics
75	   opt-in prompt as part of this same flow; accept it.
76	5. **Expect**: proceeds to Home/Chat. Confirm in the backend (or a debug log of the request) that
77	   `PATCH account-settings-update` was called with `{"biometricEnabled": true}`.
78	6. Force-quit the Simulator mid-way through step 3 (after the first PIN entry, before
79	   confirmation) and relaunch. **Expect**: the PIN setup flow resumes (not a stuck/PIN-less state,
80	   not routed to Home/Chat).
81	
82	### Story 4 — Recover via full login (P3)
83	
84	1. From the vault screen (biometric or PIN state), tap "usar e-mail e senha".
85	2. **Expect**: the existing F000 login/sign-up screen opens.
86	3. Submit valid credentials. **Expect**: proceeds into the app the same way a fresh login would
87	   (i.e., through the vault gate again if a PIN is already configured on this device — see
88	   data-model.md's gatekeeper transition for `LoginSignupPage`'s success branch).
89	
90	### Edge cases worth exercising manually at least once
91	
92	- Simulator **Features → Face ID → Enrolled** turned back off between launches → vault should show
93	  the PIN keypad directly on the next open, no fingerprint prompt attempted, no error about missing
94	  hardware.
95	- Offline device (Simulator network link conditioner, or airplane mode) during step 4–5 of Story
96	  3 → PIN setup still completes and reaches Home/Chat; only the backend write silently fails.

  contracts/biometrics-preference-repository.md.

## Manual verification (device/Simulator — `local_auth` has no platform channel under `flutter_test`)

The iOS Simulator supports Face ID without real hardware: **Features → Face ID → Enrolled**, then
**Features → Face ID → Matching Face** / **Non-matching Face** to simulate a pass/fail scan on
demand.

### Story 1 — Unlock with Face ID/Touch ID (P1)

1. Enroll Face ID in the Simulator; complete sign-up once (Story 3 flow below) with the biometric
   opt-in accepted.
2. Force-quit and relaunch the app (cold launch).
3. **Expect**: Splash → vault screen with the fingerprint prompt, before any Home/Chat content
   renders. **Features → Face ID → Matching Face** → app proceeds straight to Home/Chat.
4. Background the app (Simulator: Cmd+Shift+H or Device → Home), wait 5+ minutes (or temporarily
   lower the constant in a local-only debug build to verify the mechanism faster, then revert),
   bring it back. **Expect**: vault screen re-appears over Home/Chat; matching Face ID again
   reveals Home/Chat exactly as left (scroll position, any in-progress state).
5. Repeat the same background/resume but under 5 minutes. **Expect**: no vault screen, Home/Chat
   is immediately interactive.

### Story 2 — Biometric failure falls back to PIN (P1)

1. From the vault screen's fingerprint prompt, **Features → Face ID → Non-matching Face**.
2. **Expect**: PIN keypad appears immediately with "Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN".
3. Enter the correct 4-digit PIN. **Expect**: unlocks normally.
4. Repeat; enter an incorrect PIN. **Expect**: digits clear, error state remains, no limit —
   retry with the correct PIN still works afterward.

### Story 3 — First-time PIN setup (P2)

1. Delete the app (or clear its Keychain data) to guarantee no PIN/session exists; launch fresh.
2. Sign up with a new email. **Expect**: immediately after signup succeeds, the create-PIN screen
   appears (not Home/Chat) — 4 progress dots, 3×4 keypad.
3. Enter 4 digits; **expect** the confirmation step. Enter a *different* 4 digits. **Expect**: clear
   mismatch message, returned to entering a new PIN, nothing saved yet.
4. Enter and confirm matching PINs. If the Simulator has Face ID enrolled, **expect** a biometrics
   opt-in prompt as part of this same flow; accept it.
5. **Expect**: proceeds to Home/Chat. Confirm in the backend (or a debug log of the request) that
   `PATCH account-settings-update` was called with `{"biometricEnabled": true}`.
6. Force-quit the Simulator mid-way through step 3 (after the first PIN entry, before
   confirmation) and relaunch. **Expect**: the PIN setup flow resumes (not a stuck/PIN-less state,
   not routed to Home/Chat).

1. From the vault screen (biometric or PIN state), tap "usar e-mail e senha".
2. **Expect**: the existing F000 login/sign-up screen opens.
3. Submit valid credentials. **Expect**: proceeds into the app the same way a fresh login would
   (i.e., through the vault gate again if a PIN is already configured on this device — see
   data-model.md's gatekeeper transition for `LoginSignupPage`'s success branch).

- Simulator **Features → Face ID → Enrolled** turned back off between launches → vault should show
  the PIN keypad directly on the next open, no fingerprint prompt attempted, no error about missing
  hardware.
- Offline device (Simulator network link conditioner, or airplane mode) during step 4–5 of Story
  3 → PIN setup still completes and reaches Home/Chat; only the backend write silently fails.

# Contract: `VaultRepository` (`lib/features/vault/domain/repositories/vault_repository.dart`)

Domain-layer interface owning everything local to the device: PIN storage/verification, biometric
hardware capability, the local biometrics-preference mirror, and the in-memory relock timestamp.
`VaultBloc` and the lifecycle observer depend on this and on nothing in `vault/data/` directly
(RNF06). Registered as a `get_it` `lazySingleton` — one instance for the app's process lifetime,
which is what lets `lastUnlockedAt`/`backgroundedAt` survive navigation without a database
(data-model.md Vault Lock State).

```dart
abstract class VaultRepository {
  // Device PIN
  Future<bool> hasPinConfigured();
  Future<void> savePin(String pin);          // hashes internally (research.md R2); overwrites any prior value
  Future<bool> verifyPin(String pin);         // hashes the input, compares to the stored digest

  // Biometric capability (local_auth never crosses this boundary — see data-model.md)
  Future<BiometricCapability> checkBiometricCapability();
  Future<BiometricAuthOutcome> attemptBiometricAuth();   // success | failed | cancelled | notAvailable

  // Local biometrics-preference mirror (NOT the backend's copy — research.md R6)
  Future<bool> isBiometricPreferenceEnabled();
  Future<void> setBiometricPreferenceLocally(bool enabled);

  // Vault Lock State (in-memory only, data-model.md)
  void recordBackgrounded(DateTime at);
  DateTime? consumeBackgroundedAt();          // reads then clears, so one resume only ever evaluates once
  void markUnlocked(DateTime at);
  DateTime? get lastUnlockedAt;
}
```

- **`hasPinConfigured`/`savePin`/`verifyPin`** → back `DetermineVaultEntryUseCase`,
  `SavePinUseCase`, `VerifyPinUseCase`. None return `Either<Failure, T>` — research.md R5 covers
  why a local hash mismatch or "no PIN yet" is not a backend-taxonomy `Failure`.
- **`checkBiometricCapability`** → called once per `VaultPage` open (not cached across process
  lifetime, since the Edge Cases require detecting an OS-level biometric change *between*
  sessions — e.g. the user disabled Face ID in iOS Settings since the last launch).
- **`attemptBiometricAuth`** → wraps `LocalAuthBiometricDataSource.authenticate(biometricOnly:
  true)` (research.md R1); `cancelled`, `failed`, and `notAvailable` are all routed to the same
  PIN-fallback UI by `VaultBloc` (FR-004 does not distinguish "not recognized" from "user tapped
  away" from "biometrics became unavailable mid-attempt" — e.g. an iOS biometric lockout after
  repeated failures, or the OS capability changing between `DetermineVaultEntryUseCase`'s check and
  the actual `authenticate()` call). `notAvailable` is a real, reachable outcome of this method even
  though `DetermineVaultEntryUseCase` only enters `unlockBiometricFirst` when capability was
  `available` moments earlier — the two calls are not atomic.
- **`isBiometricPreferenceEnabled`/`setBiometricPreferenceLocally`** → the *local* mirror
  `DetermineVaultEntryUseCase` actually reads; kept separate from `BiometricsPreferenceRepository`
  (which only ever writes to the backend, never reads) per research.md R6.
- **`recordBackgrounded`/`consumeBackgroundedAt`** → `VaultLifecycleObserver` calls these directly
  on pause/resume; `consumeBackgroundedAt` clears the stored value so a second rapid resume isn't
  double-counted against a background period that's already been evaluated.
- **`markUnlocked`/`lastUnlockedAt`** → `lastUnlockedAt` exists for observability/tests; the actual
  relock decision only needs `backgroundedAt` vs. "now" (data-model.md's
  `EvaluateBackgroundResumeUseCase`), not a comparison against `lastUnlockedAt` — the background
  gap itself is what's timed, not time-since-unlock, so a user who re-locks, re-unlocks, then
  backgrounds again immediately starts a fresh gap correctly.

## `DetermineVaultEntryUseCase` (orchestration, domain layer)

```dart
Future<VaultEntryMode> call() async {
  if (!await repo.hasPinConfigured()) return VaultEntryMode.pinSetupRequired;

  final capability = await repo.checkBiometricCapability();
  final preferred = await repo.isBiometricPreferenceEnabled();
  return (capability == BiometricCapability.available && preferred)
      ? VaultEntryMode.unlockBiometricFirst
      : VaultEntryMode.unlockPinOnly;
}
```

This is the only place FR-003's "attempt biometrics first when enabled and available, otherwise go
straight to PIN" rule is implemented — `VaultBloc` calls it once per `VaultPage` open and never
re-derives the branching itself.

## Who depends on this

`VaultBloc` (both setup and unlock sub-states), `VaultLifecycleObserver` (background/resume
timing), `SaveBiometricsPreferenceUseCase` (writes the local mirror before firing the backend
call). No `presentation/` widget calls `VaultRepository` directly — always through a usecase or
through `VaultBloc`.
